title.zh: 卷三百二十五 列傳第八十四 劉平 任福 王珪 武英 桑懌 耿傅 王仲寶
title.en: Volume 325 Biographies 84: Liu Ping, Ren Fu, Wang Gui, Wu Ying, Sang Yi, Geng Fu, Wang Zhongbao
title.raw: 卷三百二十五 列傳第八十四 劉平 任福 王珪 武英 桑懌 耿傅 王仲寶 Volume 325 Biographies 84: Liu Ping, Ren Fu, Wang Gui, Wu Ying, Sang Yi, Geng Fu, Wang Zhongbao

sentences.zh: 劉平，字士衡，開封祥符人。

translations.literal: Liu Ping, styled Shiheng, was a man of Xiangfu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ping, whose courtesy name was Shiheng, came from Xiangfu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父漢凝，從太宗征河東岢嵐、憲州，累遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: His father Han Ning followed Taizong in campaigns against Ke'en and Xian in Hedong, and was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Liu Haining had followed Emperor Taizong in the conquest of Ke'en and Xian in Hedong and rose through repeated promotions to the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 平剛直任俠，善弓馬，讀書強記。

translations.literal: Ping was upright and chivalrous, skilled in bow and horse, and had a powerful memory for reading.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was forthright and fond of chivalrous deeds; he excelled at archery and horsemanship and read with an unusually retentive memory.

sentences.zh: 進士及第，補無錫尉，擊賊殺五人，擢大理評事。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was appointed assistant magistrate of Wuxi, killed five bandits in combat, and was promoted to Case Reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: After passing the jinshi examination he served as assistant magistrate of Wuxi, slew five bandits in a fight, and was promoted to case reviewer in the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 知鄢陵縣，徙南充。

translations.literal: He governed Yanling County and was transferred to Nanchong.
translations.idiomatic: He was magistrate of Yanling County and was later transferred to Nanchong.

sentences.zh: 夷人寇淯井監，轉運使以平權瀘州事，平率土丁三千擊走之。

translations.literal: The barbarians raided the Yu Well Salt Office; the transport commissioner put Ping in charge of Luzhou affairs, and Ping led three thousand local militia to drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribesmen raided the Yu Well salt office, the transport commissioner placed Ping in charge of Luzhou; Ping led three thousand local militiamen and repulsed them.

sentences.zh: 祠汾陰，遷本寺丞。

translations.literal: When sacrifices were offered at Fenyin, he was promoted to Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: After taking part in the Fenyin sacrifices, he was promoted to registrar in the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 還，路由安州，遇賊十數人，平發矢斃三賊，餘駭散。

translations.literal: On his return, his route passed through An Prefecture; he met a dozen-odd bandits, shot three dead with arrows, and the rest fled in alarm.
translations.idiomatic: On the journey home his route passed through An Prefecture, where he met a band of about a dozen robbers; he shot three dead with his bow, and the rest scattered in fright.

sentences.zh: 以寇準薦，為殿中丞、知瀘州，夷人懲前敗，不敢擾邊。

translations.literal: On Kou Zhun's recommendation he became Palace Attendant and prefect of Luzhou; the barbarians, chastened by their earlier defeat, did not dare disturb the border.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended by Kou Zhun, he was made palace attendant and prefect of Luzhou; the tribesmen, mindful of their earlier defeat, no longer dared trouble the frontier.

sentences.zh: 召拜監察御史，數上疏論事，為丁謂所忌。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Investigating Censor, repeatedly memorializing on affairs of state, and was resented by Ding Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the post of investigating censor and submitted many memorials on state affairs, which earned him the enmity of Ding Wei.

sentences.zh: 久之，除三司鹽鐵判官、河北安撫，改殿中侍御史、陝西轉運使。

translations.literal: After some time he was made Salt and Iron Commissioner of the Three Departments and Hebei Pacification Commissioner, then changed to Attending Censor in the Palace and Shaanxi Transport Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was appointed salt and iron commissioner of the Three Departments and pacification commissioner for Hebei, then transferred to attending censor in the palace and transport commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 與副使論事不合，徙知襄州。

translations.literal: He disagreed with the deputy commissioner on policy and was transferred to govern Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When he and the deputy commissioner could not agree on policy, he was transferred to serve as prefect of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷侍御史。

translations.literal: When Renzong took the throne, he was promoted to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong ascended the throne, Ping was promoted to attending censor.

sentences.zh: 初，真宗知其才，將用之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Zhenzong knew his talent and was about to employ him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Emperor Zhenzong had recognized his ability and was on the point of giving him high office.

sentences.zh: 丁謂乘間曰：「平，將家子，素知兵，若使將西北，可以制敵。

translations.literal: Ding Wei seized an opportunity and said: "Ping is the son of a military family and has long known warfare; if he is made commander in the northwest, he can control the enemy."
translations.idiomatic: Ding Wei seized his chance and said, "Ping comes from a military family and has long understood warfare; if he is sent to command in the northwest, he can keep the enemy in check."

sentences.zh: 」後章獻太后思謂言，特改衣庫使、知邠州。

translations.literal: " Later the Empress Dowager Zhangxian recalled Ding Wei's words and specially changed Ping to Wardrobe Keeper and prefect of Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Empress Dowager Zhangxian, recalling Ding Wei's remark, had him made wardrobe keeper and prefect of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 屬戶明珠、磨糜族數反覆，平潛兵殺數千人，以功領賓州刺史、鄜延路兵馬鈐轄，徙涇原路，兼知渭州。

translations.literal: When the Hu Mingzhu and Momi tribes repeatedly rebelled, Ping sent troops in secret and killed several thousand; for this merit he headed Bin Prefecture as prefect and military superintendent of the Fuyan Circuit, was moved to the Jingyuan Circuit, and concurrently governed Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hu Mingzhu and Momi clans rose again and again, Ping sent troops in secret and killed several thousand of them; for this he was made prefect of Binzhou and military superintendent on the Fuyan circuit, then transferred to the Jingyuan circuit while also governing Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 胡則為陝西都轉運使，平奏曰：「則，丁謂黨，今隸則部，慮掎摭致罪。

translations.literal: Hu Ze became overall transport commissioner of Shaanxi; Ping memorialized: "Ze is of Ding Wei's faction; I now fall under Ze's jurisdiction and fear he will seize on faults to bring charges against me."
translations.idiomatic: When Hu Ze became overall transport commissioner for Shaanxi, Ping memorialized, "Ze belongs to Ding Wei's faction; I now serve under him and fear he will find pretexts to bring charges against me."

sentences.zh: 」徙汝州，改淮南、江浙、荊湖制置發運副使，行數驛，召還，真拜信州刺史、知雄州。

translations.literal: " He was transferred to Ru Prefecture, then made deputy commissioner for transport in Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu; after several post-stations he was recalled and formally appointed prefect of Xin Prefecture and governor of Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ruzhou, then made deputy transport commissioner for Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu; after traveling several stages he was recalled and formally appointed prefect of Xinzhou and military governor of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 居四年，遷忻州團練使、知成德軍。

translations.literal: After four years he was promoted to regimental trainer of Xin Prefecture and governor of the Chengde army.
translations.idiomatic: After four years he was promoted to regimental trainer of Xinzhou and governor of the Chengde army.

sentences.zh: 時呂夷簡為宰相，臺諫官數言政事闕失，平奏書曰：「臣見范仲淹等毀訾大臣，此必有要人授旨仲淹輩，欲逐大臣而代其位者。

translations.literal: At the time Lü Yijian was chief minister; censors and remonstrators repeatedly spoke of governmental failings. Ping submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant sees Fan Zhongyan and others slandering great ministers; there must be an important person instructing Fan Zhongyan's group, wishing to drive out great ministers and take their places."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Lü Yijian was chief minister, and the censorate and remonstrance officials were repeatedly criticizing lapses in government. Ping submitted a memorial: "I see Fan Zhongyan and others vilifying senior ministers; some powerful figure must be directing them, intending to drive those ministers out and take their posts."

sentences.zh: 臣於真宗朝為御史，顧當時同列，未聞有奸邪黨與詐忠賣直，所為若此。

translations.literal: Your servant served as censor in Zhenzong's reign; looking back at my colleagues then, I never heard of wicked factions feigning loyalty and selling integrity, acting as these men do.
translations.idiomatic: I served as a censor under Emperor Zhenzong, and among my colleagues at that time I never heard of factions of the wicked feigning loyalty and parading their integrity in this fashion.

sentences.zh: 臣慮小臣以淺文薄伎，偶致顯用，不識朝廷典故，而論事浸淫，遂及管軍將校。

translations.literal: Your servant fears that petty officials, with shallow learning and slight skills, may by chance rise to prominence, not know court precedent, and in discussing affairs gradually encroach until they reach commanders and officers who manage troops.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that minor officials of shallow learning and slight talent may by chance rise to prominence without understanding court precedent, and that their criticisms will spread until they reach the commanders and officers who manage the armies.

sentences.zh: 且武人進退，與儒臣異路，若掎摭短長，妄有舉劾，則心搖而怨結矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, the advancement and dismissal of military men follows a different path from civil officials; if one seizes on their faults and strengths and recklessly impeaches them, hearts will waver and resentments will form.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the promotion and dismissal of military men follows a different path from that of civil officials; if one seizes on their faults and recklessly impeaches them, their loyalty will waver and resentment will take root.

sentences.zh: 願明諭臺諫官，毋令越職，仍不許更相引薦。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty clearly to instruct the censors and remonstrators not to exceed their duties, and still not to allow them to recommend one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Your Majesty clearly instruct the censors and remonstrators not to exceed their duties and forbid them to recommend one another in turn.

sentences.zh: 或闕員，則朝廷自擇忠純耆德用之。

translations.literal: If there are vacancies, then the court itself should select loyal, pure, and venerable men to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: When vacancies arise, the court itself should choose loyal, upright, and venerable men to fill them.

sentences.zh: 」論者以謂希夷簡意也。

translations.literal: " Commentators held that this flattered Lü Yijian's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that the memorial was meant to please Lü Yijian.

sentences.zh: 改高陽關副總管。

translations.literal: He was changed to deputy overall commander of Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to deputy overall commander at Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 寶元元年，以殿前都虞候為環慶路馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoyuan he served as chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and as deputy overall commander of infantry and cavalry on the Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Baoyuan (1038) he was made chief adjutant of the Palace Front Command and deputy overall commander of infantry and cavalry on the Huanqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 會元昊反，遷邕州觀察使，為鄜延路副總管兼鄜延、環慶路同安撫使。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Yong Prefecture, made deputy overall commander of the Fuyan Circuit and concurrent pacification commissioner of the Fuyan and Huanqing circuits.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of Yongzhou, made deputy overall commander on the Fuyan circuit, and concurrently pacification commissioner for the Fuyan and Huanqing circuits.

sentences.zh: 頃之，兼管勾涇原路兵馬，進步軍副都指揮使、靜江軍節度觀察留後。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he concurrently supervised troops of the Jingyuan Circuit, and was advanced to deputy commander-in-chief of the infantry and military governor-in-waiting of the Jingjiang army.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was also placed in charge of troops on the Jingyuan circuit and promoted to deputy commander-in-chief of the infantry and military governor-in-waiting of the Jingjiang army.

sentences.zh: 獻攻守之策曰：

translations.literal: He submitted a strategy for attack and defense, saying:
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a strategy for offense and defense, which read:

sentences.zh: 「五代之末，中國多事，唯制西戎為得之。

translations.literal: "At the end of the Five Dynasties China had many troubles; only in controlling the Western Rong did it succeed.
translations.idiomatic: "At the end of the Five Dynasties the central realm was beset by troubles everywhere, yet only in dealing with the Western Rong did it get matters right.

sentences.zh: 中國未嘗遣一騎一卒，遠屯塞上，但任土豪為眾所伏者，封以州邑，征賦所入，足以贍兵養士，由是無邊鄙之虞。

translations.literal: China never sent a single rider or soldier to garrison the distant frontier; it only entrusted local strongmen whom the masses obeyed, enfeoffing them with prefectures and districts; the revenue from levies was enough to support troops and nourish officers, and thus there was no worry on the borders.
translations.idiomatic: The court never sent a single rider or soldier to garrison the distant frontier. It simply entrusted local strongmen whom the people obeyed, enfeoffing them with prefectures and districts; the revenue from their levies was enough to support troops and officers, and the borders were left untroubled.

sentences.zh: 太祖定天下，懲唐末藩鎮之盛，削其兵柄，收其賦入，自節度以下，第坐給奉祿，或方面有警，則總師出討，事已，則兵歸宿衛，將還本鎮。

translations.literal: Taizu settled the realm, taking warning from the strength of late-Tang military governors; he cut their military authority and collected their revenues. From military governors downward they merely sat receiving stipends; if a region had an alarm, the overall commander went out to campaign; when the affair was done, the troops returned to the capital guard and the generals to their original commands.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu pacified the realm he took warning from the power of the late Tang military governors, stripped them of military authority, and collected their revenues into the central treasury. From the rank of military governor downward they merely received stipends; when a region was threatened the overall commander marched out to campaign, and when the affair was settled the troops returned to the capital guard and the generals to their home commands.

sentences.zh: 彼邊方世襲，宜異於此，而誤以朔方李彝興、靈武馮繼業一切亦徙內地。

translations.literal: Those frontier regions with hereditary succession ought to have differed from this, yet by mistake Li Yixing of Shuofang and Feng Jiye of Lingwu were likewise moved inland.
translations.idiomatic: The frontier domains with hereditary succession ought to have been treated differently, yet by mistake Li Yixing of Shuofang and Feng Jiye of Lingwu were likewise transferred inland.

sentences.zh: 自此靈、夏仰中國戍守，千里運糧，兵民並困。

translations.literal: From this time Ling and Xia relied on Chinese garrisons; grain was transported a thousand li, and soldiers and people alike were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: From that time Ling and Xia depended on Chinese garrisons; grain had to be hauled a thousand li, and both soldiers and civilians were worn down.

sentences.zh: 其後靈武失守，而趙德明懼王師問罪，願為藩臣。

translations.literal: Later Lingwu was lost, and Zhao Deming, fearing the royal army would call him to account, wished to become a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Later Lingwu fell, and Zhao Deming, fearing punishment by the imperial army, offered to become a vassal.

sentences.zh: 於時若止棄靈、夏、綏、銀，與之限山為界，則無今日之患矣。

translations.literal: At that time if we had only abandoned Ling, Xia, Sui, and Yin and set the mountains as our boundary with them, there would be no trouble of today.
translations.idiomatic: If at that time the court had simply abandoned Ling, Xia, Sui, and Yin and taken the mountains as the boundary, there would be no trouble of today.

sentences.zh: 而以靈、夏兩州及山界蕃漢戶並授德明，故蓄甲治兵，漸窺邊隙，鄜延、環慶、涇原、秦隴所以不能弛備也。

translations.literal: Yet the two prefectures of Ling and Xia and the barbarian and Chinese households of the mountain frontier were all granted to Deming; therefore he stored armor and trained troops, gradually spying on border openings, and Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, and Qin-Long could not relax their defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the two prefectures of Ling and Xia and the barbarian and Chinese households along the mountain frontier were all handed to Deming, so he gathered arms and trained troops and gradually probed the border; that is why the Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, and Qin-Long circuits cannot relax their defenses.

sentences.zh: 今元昊嗣國，政刑慘酷，眾叛親離，復與唃廝囉構怨，此乃天亡之時。

translations.literal: Now Yuan Hao has succeeded to the state; government and punishments are cruel, the masses rebel and kin turn away, and he has again made enmity with Gusiluo—this is the time Heaven will destroy him.
translations.idiomatic: Now Yuan Hao has succeeded to the throne; his rule and punishments are brutal, his subjects and kin have turned against him, and he is again at odds with Gusiluo—this is the moment Heaven is ready to destroy him.

sentences.zh: 臣聞寇不可玩，敵不可縱。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that bandits must not be trifled with and enemies must not be indulged.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that bandits must not be trifled with and enemies must not be indulged.

sentences.zh: 或元昊不能自立，別有酋豪代之，西與唃廝囉復平，北約契丹為表裏，則何以制其侵軼？

translations.literal: Or if Yuan Hao cannot hold himself, another tribal chief replaces him, makes peace again with Gusiluo in the west, and allies with the Khitan in the north as inner and outer support—how then can we control their raids?
translations.idiomatic: If Yuan Hao cannot hold power and another tribal leader replaces him, makes peace with Gusiluo in the west, and allies with the Khitan in the north as mutual support, how will we restrain their raids?

sentences.zh: 今元昊國勢未強，若乘此用鄜延、環慶、涇原、秦隴四路兵馬，分兩道，益以蕃漢弓箭手，精兵可得二十萬，三倍元昊之眾，轉糧二百里，不出一月，可收山界洪、宥等州。

translations.literal: Now Yuan Hao's state power is not yet strong; if we seize this moment and use the troops of the four circuits Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, and Qin-Long, dividing into two routes and adding barbarian and Chinese archers, elite troops can reach two hundred thousand—three times Yuan Hao's host; transporting grain two hundred li, within one month we can recover the mountain-border prefectures Hong, You, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao's power is not yet firm; if we seize this moment and deploy the armies of the Fuyan, Huanqing, Jingyuan, and Qin-Long circuits in two columns, reinforced by barbarian and Chinese archers, we can field two hundred thousand picked troops—three times Yuan Hao's strength. With supplies carried only two hundred li, within a month we can recover the mountain-border prefectures Hong, You, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 招集土豪，縻之以職，自防禦使以下、刺史以上，第封之，給以衣祿金帛；

translations.literal: Summon local strongmen and tether them with offices; from defense commissioner downward and prefect upward, enfeoff them in order and grant robes, stipends, gold, and silk;
translations.idiomatic: Summon the local strongmen and bind them with office, enfeoffing them in rank from defense commissioner down to prefect and granting robes, stipends, gold, and silk;

sentences.zh: 又以土人補將校，使勇者貪於祿，富者安於家，不期月而人心自定。

translations.literal: also fill officer posts with natives, so the brave covet stipends and the wealthy rest content at home—in less than a month popular sentiment will settle of itself.
translations.idiomatic: and fill officer posts with local men so that the brave are drawn by stipends and the wealthy are content at home; in less than a month the people will settle of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 及遣使諭唃廝囉，授以靈武節度，使撓河外族帳，以窘元昊。

translations.literal: Then send envoys to instruct Gusiluo, grant him the Lingwu command, and have him harass the tribal encampments beyond the river to distress Yuan Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Then send envoys to Gusiluo, grant him the Lingwu command, and have him harass the tribal encampments beyond the river to press Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 復出麟、府、石州蕃漢步騎，獵取河西部族，招其酋帥，離其部眾，然後以大軍繼之，元昊不過鼠竄為窮寇爾，何所為哉！

translations.literal: Again send out barbarian and Chinese infantry and cavalry of Lin, Fu, and Shi prefectures to hunt the tribes west of the river, win over their chiefs, and divide their followers; then follow with the great army—Yuan Hao will be no more than a rat scurrying as a cornered bandit; what can he do!
translations.idiomatic: Then send out the barbarian and Chinese infantry and cavalry of Lin, Fu, and Shi to harry the tribes west of the river, win over their chiefs, and split their followers; when the main army follows, Yuan Hao will be no more than a rat scurrying before a beaten foe—what can he do?

sentences.zh: 且靈、夏、綏、銀地不產五穀，人不習險阻，每歲資糧，取足洪、宥。

translations.literal: Moreover, the lands of Ling, Xia, Sui, and Yin produce no grain; the people are unused to rugged terrain; each year's provisions are drawn fully from Hong and You.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Ling, Xia, Sui, and Yin produce no grain, their people are unused to rugged country, and each year's provisions are drawn entirely from Hong and You.

sentences.zh: 而洪、宥州羌戶勁勇善戰，夏人恃此以為肘腋。

translations.literal: The Qiang households of Hong and You prefectures are stalwart and skilled in battle; the Xia people rely on them as armpit and flank.
translations.idiomatic: The Qiang households of Hong and You are fierce fighters, and the Xia depend on them as their right arm.

sentences.zh: 我苟得之，以山為界，憑高據險，下瞰沙漠，各列堡障，量以戎兵鎮守，此天險也。

translations.literal: If we gain them, take the mountains as boundary, hold the heights and occupy the passes, look down on the desert below, set out fortresses and barriers at each point, and post frontier troops in measured garrisons—this is Heaven's strategic terrain.
translations.idiomatic: If we take them, set the mountains as our boundary, hold the heights and the passes, look down on the desert below, and post frontier troops in measured garrisons at each strongpoint—this is terrain Heaven itself has made defensible.

sentences.zh: 廟朝之謀，不知出此，而爭靈、夏、綏、銀，連年調發，老師費財，以致中國疲弊，小醜猖獗，此議臣之罪也。

translations.literal: The court's counsels did not know to adopt this, but contended for Ling, Xia, Sui, and Yin year after year with levies and deployments, wearing out the army and wasting treasure until China was exhausted and a petty villain ran riot—this fault lies with the ministers who urged such counsel.
translations.idiomatic: The court's counsellors did not see this course, but year after year fought over Ling, Xia, Sui, and Yin, wearing out the armies and draining the treasury until the realm was exhausted and a petty rebel ran wild—the fault lies with the ministers who urged that policy.

sentences.zh: 今朝廷或貸元昊罪，更示含容，不惟宿兵轉多，經費尤甚。

translations.literal: Now the court may pardon Yuan Hao's crime and show further forbearance—not only will garrison troops increase, but expenditures will be still greater.
translations.idiomatic: If the court now pardons Yuan Hao and shows further forbearance, garrison troops will only increase and expenditures grow still heavier.

sentences.zh: 萬一元昊潛結契丹，互為掎角，則我一身二疾，不可並治。

translations.literal: If by chance Yuan Hao secretly joins the Khitan in mutual pincer support, then we have two ailments in one body and cannot treat them together.
translations.idiomatic: If Yuan Hao secretly allies with the Khitan in mutual support, we shall have two ailments in one body and cannot treat them at once.

sentences.zh: 必輕者為先，重者為後，如何減兵以應河北？

translations.literal: The lighter must be handled first and the heavier after—how then can troops be reduced to meet Hebei?
translations.idiomatic: The lesser threat must be dealt with first and the greater afterward—how then can we reduce troops to meet the danger in Hebei?

sentences.zh: 請召邊臣，與二府定守禦長策。」

translations.literal: I beg that frontier officials be summoned to settle with the Two Departments a long-term plan for defense."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that frontier officials be summoned to work with the Two Departments on a long-term plan for defense."

sentences.zh: 疏奏未報。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted but no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but no reply came.

sentences.zh: 屬元昊盛兵攻保安軍，時平屯慶州，范雍以書召平，平率兵與石元孫合軍趨土門。

translations.literal: Just then Yuan Hao massed troops to attack Bao'an army; Ping was then stationed at Qing Prefecture; Fan Yong summoned him by letter; Ping led troops and joined Shi Yuansun's army, hurrying toward Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Yuan Hao massed his army against Bao'an; Ping was stationed at Qingzhou when Fan Yong summoned him by letter. Ping led his troops to join Shi Yuansun and marched toward Tumen.

sentences.zh: 既又有告敵兵破金明、圍延州者，雍復召平與元孫救延州。

translations.literal: Then there came word that the enemy had taken Jinming and besieged Yan Prefecture; Yong again summoned Ping and Yuansun to rescue Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Then word came that the enemy had taken Jinming and was besieging Yanzhou, and Yong again summoned Ping and Yuansun to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 平素輕敵，督騎兵晝夜倍道行，明日，至萬安鎮。

translations.literal: Ping had always underestimated the enemy; he drove the cavalry day and night at double march, and the next day reached Wan'an town.
translations.idiomatic: Ping had always held the enemy lightly in esteem; he drove his cavalry day and night at forced march and reached Wan'an the next day.

sentences.zh: 平先發，步軍繼進，夜至三川口西十里止營，遣騎兵先趨延州爭門。

translations.literal: Ping set out first and the infantry followed; at night they halted camp ten li west of Sanchuan Ford and sent cavalry ahead to race for Yanzhou and seize the gates.
translations.idiomatic: Ping marched ahead while the infantry followed; that night they camped ten li west of Sanchuan Ford and sent cavalry ahead to seize the gates of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 時鄜延路駐泊都監黃德和將二千餘人，屯保安北碎金谷，巡檢万俟政、郭遵各將所部分屯，范雍皆召之為外援，平亦使人趣其行。

translations.literal: At the time Huang Dehe, garrison commander of the Fuyan Circuit, led more than two thousand men and was stationed at Suijin Valley north of Bao'an; inspectors Moqi Zheng and Guo Zun each led their detachments in separate camps; Fan Yong summoned them all as outside aid, and Ping also sent men to urge them on.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Dehe, garrison commander on the Fuyan circuit, had more than two thousand men at Suijin Valley north of Bao'an; inspectors Moqi Zheng and Guo Zun held separate camps with their detachments. Fan Yong summoned them all as reinforcements, and Ping also sent men to hurry them forward.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，步兵未至，平與元孫還逆之。

translations.literal: At dawn the infantry had not arrived; Ping and Yuansun turned back to meet them.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the infantry had not yet arrived, and Ping and Yuansun turned back to meet them.

sentences.zh: 行二十里，乃遇步兵，及德和、万俟政、郭遵所將兵悉至，將步騎萬餘結陣東行五里，與敵遇。

translations.literal: After marching twenty li they met the infantry, and the troops led by Dehe, Moqi Zheng, and Guo Zun all arrived; with more than ten thousand infantry and cavalry they formed battle lines and marched east five li, then met the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty li they met the infantry, and the forces of Dehe, Moqi Zheng, and Guo Zun all came up; with more than ten thousand foot and horse they formed ranks and marched east five li before meeting the enemy.

sentences.zh: 時平地雪數寸，平與敵皆為偃月陣相向。

translations.literal: Snow on the level ground was several inches deep; Ping and the enemy both formed crescent arrays facing each other.
translations.idiomatic: Snow lay several inches deep on the plain; Ping and the enemy both drew up in crescent formations facing one another.

sentences.zh: 有頃，敵兵涉水為橫陣，郭遵及忠佐王信薄之，不能入。

translations.literal: After a while the enemy crossed the water and formed a horizontal array; Guo Zun and loyal aide Wang Xin pressed them but could not break in.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the enemy crossed the stream and formed a line; Guo Zun and loyal aide Wang Xin charged them but could not break through.

sentences.zh: 官軍並進，殺數百人，乃退。

translations.literal: The government army advanced together, killed several hundred men, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops advanced together, killed several hundred of the enemy, and then fell back.

sentences.zh: 敵復蔽盾為陣，官軍復擊卻之，奪盾，殺獲及溺水死者幾千人。

translations.literal: The enemy again screened themselves with shields in formation; the government army struck and drove them back, seized shields, and killed, captured, and drowned nearly several thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy again raised a shield wall; the government troops struck again and drove them back, seizing shields and killing, capturing, or drowning nearly several thousand.

sentences.zh: 平左耳、右頸中流矢。

translations.literal: Ping was struck by arrows in his left ear and right neck.
translations.idiomatic: Ping was wounded by arrows in his left ear and right neck.

sentences.zh: 日暮，戰士上首功及所獲馬，平曰：「戰方急，爾各誌之，皆當重賞汝。

translations.literal: At dusk soldiers presented heads for merit and captured horses; Ping said: "The battle is still urgent—each of you record them; you will all be richly rewarded."
translations.idiomatic: At dusk soldiers came forward with heads and captured horses for credit; Ping said, "The fight is still urgent—mark them down; you will all be richly rewarded."

sentences.zh: 」語未已，敵以輕兵薄戰，官軍引卻二十步。

translations.literal: " Before he had finished speaking, the enemy sent light troops to press the fight, and the government army drew back twenty paces.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had finished, the enemy sent light troops to press the attack, and the government army fell back twenty paces.

sentences.zh: 黃德和居陣後，望見軍卻，率麾下走保西南山，眾從之，皆潰。

translations.literal: Huang Dehe was in the rear of the formation; seeing the army fall back, he led his followers to flee and hold the southwest hills; the masses followed and all collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Dehe was in the rear; when he saw the army fall back he led his men in flight toward the southwest hills, the rest followed, and the whole force broke.

sentences.zh: 平遣其子宜孫馳追德和，執轡語曰：「當勒兵還，倂力抗敵，奈何先奔？

translations.literal: Ping sent his son Yisun in fast pursuit of Dehe, seized the reins and said: "You ought to rein in the troops and return, joining strength to resist the enemy—why flee first?"
translations.idiomatic: Ping sent his son Yisun in pursuit of Dehe, seized his reins, and said, "You should turn the troops back and fight the enemy together—why run away first?"

sentences.zh: 」德和不從，驅馬遁赴甘泉。

translations.literal: " Dehe would not obey and drove his horse in flight to Ganquan.
translations.idiomatic: Dehe would not listen and galloped away toward Ganquan.

sentences.zh: 平遣軍校杖劍遮留士卒，得千餘人。

translations.literal: Ping sent military officers with staffs and swords to block and hold the soldiers, gathering more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Ping sent officers with swords to block the fleeing soldiers and held more than a thousand men together.

sentences.zh: 轉鬥三日，賊退還水東。

translations.literal: Fighting shifted for three days; the bandits withdrew east of the water.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting continued for three days until the enemy withdrew east of the stream.

sentences.zh: 平率餘眾保西南山，立七柵自固。

translations.literal: Ping led the remaining force to hold the southwest hills and erected seven palisades to secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Ping led the survivors to the southwest hills and built seven palisaded camps to hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 敵夜使人叩柵，問大將安在，士不應。

translations.literal: At night the enemy sent men to knock on the palisades and ask where the great general was; the soldiers did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: That night the enemy sent men to knock on the palisades and ask where the commander was; the soldiers did not answer.

sentences.zh: 復使人偽為戍卒，遞文移平，平殺之。

translations.literal: They again sent men disguised as garrison soldiers to deliver documents to Ping; Ping killed them.
translations.idiomatic: They again sent men disguised as garrison troops with documents for Ping; he had them killed.

sentences.zh: 夜四鼓，敵環營呼曰：「如許殘兵，不降何待！

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night the enemy surrounded the camp and shouted: "With so few broken troops left, why not surrender!"
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch the enemy surrounded the camp and shouted, "With so few broken troops left, why not surrender!"

sentences.zh: 」平旦，敵酋舉鞭麾騎，自山四出合擊，絕官軍為二，遂與元孫皆被執。

translations.literal: " At daybreak the enemy chief raised his whip to command the horsemen; from four sides of the hills they joined in attack, cut the government army in two, and then both Ping and Yuansun were captured.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak the enemy chief raised his whip; horsemen poured from all sides of the hills, cut the government army in two, and Ping and Yuansun were both taken.

sentences.zh: 初，德和言平降賊，朝廷發禁兵圍其家。

translations.literal: At first Dehe said Ping had surrendered to the bandits; the court sent palace troops to surround his household.
translations.idiomatic: At first Dehe reported that Ping had surrendered to the enemy, and the court sent palace troops to surround his home.

sentences.zh: 及命殿中侍御史文彥博即河中府置獄，遣龐籍往訊焉，具得其實。

translations.literal: Then Attending Censor Wen Yanbo was ordered to set up a prison at Hezhong Prefecture and Pang Ji was sent to investigate; the full truth was obtained.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered attending censor Wen Yanbo to set up a tribunal at Hezhong and sent Pang Ji to investigate; the full truth came out.

sentences.zh: 遂釋其家，德和坐腰斬。

translations.literal: His household was then released, and Dehe was sentenced to execution at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Ping's family was released, and Dehe was executed by cutting in two at the waist.

sentences.zh: 而延州吏民亦詣闕訴平戰沒狀，遂贈朔方軍節度使兼侍中，諡壯武，賜信陵坊第，封其妻趙氏為南陽郡太夫人，子孫及諸弟皆優遷，未官者錄之。

translations.literal: The officials and people of Yan Prefecture also went to court to report how Ping had died in battle; he was then posthumously made military governor of the Shuofang army and concurrent palace attendant, given the posthumous title Zhuangwu, granted a residence in Xinling ward, his wife Lady Zhao was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Nanyang commandery, his sons, grandsons, and younger brothers were all preferentially promoted, and those without office were enrolled.
translations.idiomatic: The officials and people of Yanzhou also went to court to testify how Ping had died fighting; he was posthumously made military governor of the Shuofang army and concurrent palace attendant, given the posthumous title Zhuangwu, granted a residence in Xinling ward, his wife Lady Zhao was enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Nanyang commandery, and his sons, grandsons, and younger brothers were all preferentially promoted, with those without office enrolled in service.

sentences.zh: 其後降羌多言平在興州未死，生子於賊中。

translations.literal: Later many surrendered Qiang said Ping had not died at Xing Prefecture and had fathered a son among the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Later many surrendered Qiang said that Ping had not died at Xingzhou and had even fathered a son among the enemy.

sentences.zh: 及石元孫歸，乃知平戰時被執，後沒於興州。

translations.literal: When Shi Yuansun returned, it was learned that Ping had been captured in battle and later perished at Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Yuansun returned, it became known that Ping had been captured in battle and later died at Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟兼濟。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Jianji.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Jianji.

sentences.zh: 弟 兼濟

translations.literal: Younger brother: Jianji
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother: Jianji

sentences.zh: 兼濟，字寶臣，以父蔭補三班奉職。

translations.literal: Jianji, styled Baochen, entered service through his father's privilege as a third-rank attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji, whose courtesy name was Baochen, entered service through his father's privilege as a third-rank attendant.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，讀兵書知大旨。

translations.literal: He was skilled in riding and archery and, reading military books, grasped their main points.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at riding and archery and, in reading military texts, grasped their essential points.

sentences.zh: 為襄州兵馬監押。

translations.literal: He served as military supervisor of Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as military supervisor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 漢江暴漲，兼濟解衣涉水，率眾捍城，州賴以完。

translations.literal: The Han River rose violently; Jianji stripped off his clothes, waded the water, led the masses to defend the city, and the prefecture was preserved intact thanks to him.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han River rose in flood, Jianji stripped off his clothes, waded through the water, and led the people in defending the city, so that the prefecture was saved.

sentences.zh: 擢閤門祗候、雄霸州界河巡檢，徙晉、絳、澤、潞都巡檢使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace gate attendant and frontier-river inspector of Xiong-Ba prefectures, then transferred to overall inspector of Jin, Jiang, Ze, and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace gate attendant and inspector on the frontier river of Xiong-Ba, then transferred to overall inspector for Jin, Jiang, Ze, and Lu.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，太行多盜，禽二百餘人。

translations.literal: In a year of famine there were many bandits on the Taihang range; he captured more than two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: In a famine year bandits were numerous on the Taihang range; he captured more than two hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 改左侍禁、鄜延路兵馬都監，權知保安軍，歷同提點陝西、河東刑獄，徙知籠竿城。

translations.literal: He was changed to left palace guard, overall military supervisor of the Fuyan Circuit, acting governor of Bao'an army, served as concurrent judicial intendant of Shaanxi and Hedong, and was transferred to govern Longgan city.
translations.idiomatic: He was made left palace guard and overall military supervisor on the Fuyan circuit, acted as commander of Bao'an, served as concurrent judicial intendant for Shaanxi and Hedong, and was transferred to govern Longgan.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇邊，眾號數萬，兼濟將兵千餘，轉戰至黑松林，敗之。

translations.literal: The Xia raided the border; their force was said to number tens of thousands; Jianji led a little more than a thousand troops, fought in shifts to Black Pine Forest, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided the frontier with a force said to number tens of thousands, Jianji led a little more than a thousand men, fought his way to Black Pine Forest, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 屬其兄平戰沒於三川口，特授內殿崇班、知原州。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Ping was killed in battle at Sanchuan Ford, he was specially granted Inner Palace Attendant and made prefect of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Ping was killed at Sanchuan Ford, he was specially made inner palace attendant and prefect of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 入辭，仁宗慰勉之曰：「國憂未弭，家仇未報，不可不力也。

translations.literal: On entering to take leave, Renzong comforted and exhorted him: "The state's trouble is not yet settled, your family's vengeance is not yet repaid—you must not fail to exert yourself."
translations.idiomatic: When he came to take leave, Emperor Renzong comforted him and said, "The state's trouble is not yet ended and your family's vengeance is not yet settled—you must not fail to do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 」屬戶明珠族叛，諸將欲亟討。

translations.literal: " Just then the Hu Mingzhu tribe rebelled; the generals wished to attack at once.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Hu Mingzhu clan rebelled, and the generals wanted to attack at once.

sentences.zh: 兼濟第日縱飲擊鞠，繆為不知，以疑其意。

translations.literal: Jianji daily gave himself to drinking and cuju, feigning ignorance to make them doubt his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji spent his days drinking and playing cuju, pretending not to notice so as to make the rebels suspect his intentions.

sentences.zh: 既而叛者自潰，乃追襲之，射殺其酋長，收餘眾以歸。

translations.literal: Before long the rebels collapsed of themselves; he then pursued and struck them, shot their chief dead, and gathered the remainder back.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the rebels broke up on their own; he pursued them, shot their chief dead, and brought the rest back in submission.

sentences.zh: 徙寧州，破靳廝韈砦，徙鄜州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Ning Prefecture, stormed the stockade of Jinsiwa, and was transferred to Fu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Ningzhou, stormed the Jinsiwa stockade, and was then transferred to Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊既稱藩，徙梓夔路鈐轄，又徙知鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: After Yuan Hao had submitted as a vassal, he was moved to military superintendent of the Zi-Kui Circuit and again transferred to govern Zhenrong army.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuan Hao had submitted as a vassal, he was made military superintendent on the Zi-Kui circuit and later transferred to command Zhenrong.

sentences.zh: 兼濟御下嚴急，轉運使言士心多怨，請徙諸內地。

translations.literal: Jianji governed subordinates with harsh severity; the transport commissioner said the soldiers' hearts harbored much resentment and asked that he be moved to the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Jianji ruled his men with harsh severity; the transport commissioner reported widespread resentment among the troops and asked that he be transferred inland.

sentences.zh: 改涇原路鈐轄，復知寧州，又知原州，徙冀州、廣信軍。

translations.literal: He was changed to military superintendent of the Jingyuan Circuit, again governed Ning Prefecture, also governed Yuan Prefecture, and was transferred to Ji Prefecture and Guangxin army.
translations.idiomatic: He was made military superintendent on the Jingyuan circuit, again governed Ningzhou and Yuanzhou, and was transferred to Jizhou and Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 累遷文思使、惠州刺史、河北緣邊安撫副使，擢西上閤門使、同管勾三班院，出知雄州。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Commissioner of the Literary Exchanges, prefect of Huizhou, and deputy frontier pacification commissioner of Hebei, then advanced to western upper palace gate attendant and concurrent supervisor of the Three-Rank Bureau, and sent out to govern Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of commissioner of literary exchanges, prefect of Huizhou, and deputy frontier pacification commissioner for Hebei, then was made western upper palace gate attendant and concurrent supervisor of the Three-Rank Bureau before being sent out as prefect of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，邊民避罪逃者，契丹輒納之，守將畏事不敢詰，兼濟悉移檄責還。

translations.literal: Earlier, frontier people who fled to escape punishment were readily received by the Khitan; garrison commanders feared trouble and did not press the matter; Jianji sent documents throughout demanding their return.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, frontier subjects fleeing punishment were readily sheltered by the Khitan, and garrison commanders, fearing trouble, did not press the issue; Jianji sent dispatches throughout demanding their return.

sentences.zh: 徙冀州，逾月，改忻州，復管勾三班院，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Ji Prefecture; after more than a month he was changed to Xin Prefecture, again supervised the Three-Rank Bureau, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Jizhou; after a month he was moved to Xinzhou, again supervised the Three-Rank Bureau, and died.

sentences.zh: 郭遵

translations.literal: Guo Zun
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zun

translations.literal: (Appended biography)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended biography)

sentences.zh: 郭遵者，開封人也，家世以武功稱。

translations.literal: Guo Zun was a man of Kaifeng; his family for generations was famed for martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Zun was from Kaifeng; his family had been renowned for martial prowess for generations.

sentences.zh: 遵少隸軍籍，稍遷殿前指揮使。

translations.literal: Zun early entered military rolls and was gradually promoted to commander of the Palace Front.
translations.idiomatic: Zun entered the army rolls in youth and was gradually promoted to commander of the Palace Front.

sentences.zh: 乾興中，改左班殿直、幷代路巡檢。

translations.literal: In the Qianxing era he was changed to left-rank palace attendant and inspector of the Bing-Dai Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianxing era he was made left-rank palace attendant and inspector on the Bing-Dai circuit.

sentences.zh: 遷右侍禁、慶州柔遠砦兵馬監押。

translations.literal: He was promoted to right palace guard and military supervisor of Rouyuan stockade in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to right palace guard and military supervisor at Rouyuan stockade in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 召試騎射優等，遷左侍禁、閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Summoned to trial in riding and archery with superior grade, he was promoted to left palace guard and palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Called to trial in riding and archery, he earned top marks and was made left palace guard and palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 為秦州三陽砦主，徙延州西路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: He was master of Sanyang stockade in Qin Prefecture, then transferred to overall western-route inspector of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded Sanyang stockade in Qinzhou and was later transferred to overall inspector on the western route of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇延州，遵以裨將屬劉平，遇敵，馳馬入敵陣，殺傷數十人。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao raided Yan Prefecture, Zun served as deputy general under Liu Ping; meeting the enemy, he galloped into their formation and killed or wounded several tens.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao raided Yanzhou, Zun served as a deputy under Liu Ping; meeting the enemy, he charged into their ranks on horseback and killed or wounded dozens.

sentences.zh: 敵出驍將揚言當遵，遵揮鐵杵破其腦，兩軍皆大呼。

translations.literal: The enemy sent out a fierce general who proclaimed he would take Zun; Zun swung his iron mace and shattered his skull, and both armies shouted aloud.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent out a fierce champion who boasted he would take Zun; Zun swung his iron mace and shattered his skull, and both armies roared.

sentences.zh: 復持鐵槍進，所向披靡。

translations.literal: He again took up an iron spear and advanced, scattering all before him.
translations.idiomatic: He took up an iron spear again and advanced, cutting down all who stood before him.

sentences.zh: 會黃德和引兵先潰，敵戰益急。

translations.literal: Just then Huang Dehe led his troops in flight first, and the enemy pressed the fight all the harder.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Huang Dehe broke and fled with his men, and the enemy pressed the attack all the harder.

sentences.zh: 遵奮擊，期必死，獨出入行間。

translations.literal: Zun fought fiercely, expecting certain death, going alone in and out among the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zun fought on with abandon, resolved to die, charging alone in and out of the enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 軍稍卻，即復馬以殿，又持大槊橫突之。

translations.literal: When the army fell back slightly, he at once remounted to cover the rear, then took a great spear and charged across them.
translations.idiomatic: When the army fell back he remounted to cover the rear, then took a great spear and charged across the enemy front.

sentences.zh: 敵知不可敵，使人持大絭索立高處迎遵馬，輒為遵所斷。

translations.literal: The enemy knew he could not be matched and sent men with great ropes standing on high ground to catch Zun's horse; Zun cut them through each time.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing they could not match him, the enemy posted men on high ground with great ropes to snare his horse; Zun cut through them each time.

sentences.zh: 因縱遵使深入，攢兵注射之，中馬，馬仆地，被殺。

translations.literal: They therefore let Zun go deep, then massed troops to shoot at him; his horse was hit, the horse fell, and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: They let him press deep into their lines, then massed archers and shot him down; his horse was hit and fell, and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 特贈果州團練使。

translations.literal: He was specially posthumously made regimental trainer of Guo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made regimental trainer of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 以其父斌為太子右清道率府副率；

translations.literal: His father Bin was made deputy leader of the Crown Prince's Right Clear-Way Guard;
translations.idiomatic: His father Bin was made deputy leader of the crown prince's Right Clear-Way Guard;

sentences.zh: 母賀，封仁壽郡君；

translations.literal: his mother He was enfeoffed as Lady of Renshou commandery;
translations.idiomatic: his mother He was enfeoffed as Lady of Renshou commandery;

sentences.zh: 妻尹，安康郡君；

translations.literal: his wife Yin as Lady of Ankang commandery;
translations.idiomatic: his wife Yin as Lady of Ankang commandery;

sentences.zh: 弟青石侍禁，逵三班奉職。

translations.literal: his younger brother Qingshi as palace guard, and Kui as third-rank attendant.
translations.idiomatic: his younger brother Qingshi as palace guard and Kui as third-rank attendant.

sentences.zh: 四子尚幼，仁宗悉為賜名，忠嗣西頭供奉官，忠紹左侍禁，忠裔右侍禁，忠緒左班殿直。

translations.literal: His four sons were still young; Renzong bestowed names on them all: Zhongsi as western palace supply officer, Zhongshao as left palace guard, Zhongyi as right palace guard, and Zhongxu as left-rank palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His four sons were still young; Emperor Renzong gave them all names: Zhongsi as western palace supply officer, Zhongshao as left palace guard, Zhongyi as right palace guard, and Zhongxu as left-rank palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 女舊為尼，亦賜紫方袍。

translations.literal: His daughter had formerly been a nun and was also granted a purple square robe.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter, who had formerly been a nun, was also granted a purple monastic robe.

sentences.zh: 遵用鐵杵、槍、槊、共九十斤，其後耕者得其器於戰處，皇祐中，乃倂與其衣冠葬之河南。

translations.literal: The iron mace, spear, and halberd Zun used weighed ninety jin in all; later a farmer found his weapons at the battle site; in the Huangyou era they were together with his robes and cap buried in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The iron mace, spear, and halberd he wielded weighed ninety jin together; later a farmer found them on the battlefield, and in the Huangyou era they were buried with his robes and cap in Henan.

sentences.zh: 逵，自有傳。

translations.literal: Kui has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Kui has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 任福，字祐之，其先河東人，後徙開封。

translations.literal: Ren Fu, styled Youzhi, was by origin a man of Hedong and later moved to Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu, whose courtesy name was Youzhi, came originally from Hedong and later moved to Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，補衛士，由殿前諸班累遷至遙郡刺史。

translations.literal: In the Xianping era he was enrolled as a guardsman and through the various ranks of the Palace Front was repeatedly promoted to distant-prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era he entered the guards and rose through the Palace Front ranks to distant-prefecture prefect.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，除莫州刺史、嵐石隰州緣邊都巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was made prefect of Mo Prefecture and overall frontier inspector of Lan, Shi, and Xi.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, he was made prefect of Mozhou and overall frontier inspector for Lan, Shi, and Xi.

sentences.zh: 既辭，奏曰：「河東地介大河，斥堠疏闊，願嚴守備，以戒不虞。

translations.literal: On taking leave he memorialized: "Hedong lies beside the great river; its watch-towers are few and far between—I wish strict defenses to guard against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: On taking leave he memorialized, "Hedong lies beside the Yellow River and its watch-towers are few and far between; I ask that defenses be tightened against the unforeseen."

sentences.zh: 」仁宗善之，命知隴州，擢秦鳳路馬步軍副總管。

translations.literal: " Renzong approved and ordered him to govern Long Prefecture, promoting him to deputy overall commander of infantry and cavalry on the Qinfeng Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong approved and made him prefect of Longzhou and deputy overall commander of infantry and cavalry on the Qinfeng circuit.

sentences.zh: 詔陝西增城壘、器械，福受命四十日，而戰守之備皆具。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shaanxi to add walls and engines; within forty days of receiving the command Fu had all preparations for war and defense ready.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered Shaanxi to strengthen walls and armaments, Fu received the command and within forty days had every preparation for war and defense in place.

sentences.zh: 以忻州團練使為鄜延路副總管、管勾延州東路蕃部事。

translations.literal: As regimental trainer of Xin Prefecture he became deputy overall commander of the Fuyan Circuit and supervisor of eastern-route barbarian affairs of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As regimental trainer of Xinzhou he was made deputy overall commander on the Fuyan circuit and supervisor of eastern-route tribal affairs at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 尋知慶州，復兼環慶路副總管。

translations.literal: Shortly he governed Qing Prefecture and again served concurrently as deputy overall commander of the Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he governed Qingzhou and again served as deputy overall commander on the Huanqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 上言：「慶州去蕃族不遠，願勒兵境上，按亭堡，謹斥堠。

translations.literal: He submitted: "Qing Prefecture is not far from the barbarian tribes; I wish to muster troops on the border, inspect pavilions and forts, and keep watch-towers strict."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted, "Qingzhou lies close to the tribal lands; I ask to muster troops on the border, inspect the outposts and forts, and keep the watch-towers alert."

sentences.zh: 」因經度所過山川道路，以為緩急攻守之備。

translations.literal: " He then surveyed the mountains, rivers, and roads he passed as preparations for urgent attack and defense.
translations.idiomatic: He then surveyed the mountains, rivers, and roads along his route to prepare for attack and defense in an emergency.

sentences.zh: 帝益善之，聽便宜從事。

translations.literal: The emperor approved still more and allowed him to act as circumstances required.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved still more and allowed him to act at his own discretion.

sentences.zh: 夏人寇保安、鎮戎軍，福與子懷亮、侄婿成暠自華池鳳川鎮聲言巡邊，召諸將牽制敵勢。

translations.literal: The Xia raided Bao'an and Zhenrong armies; Fu with his son Huailiang and nephew-by-marriage Cheng Gao left Huachi and Fengchuan towns proclaiming a border patrol, summoning generals to pin down the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xia raided Bao'an and Zhenrong, Fu set out from Huachi and Fengchuan with his son Huailiang and nephew-by-marriage Cheng Gao under the pretext of a border patrol and summoned the generals to pin down the enemy.

sentences.zh: 行至柔遠砦，犒蕃部，即席部分諸將，攻白豹城。

translations.literal: Reaching Rouyuan stockade, he feasted the barbarian tribes and on the spot assigned the generals to attack Baibao city.
translations.idiomatic: At Rouyuan stockade he feasted the tribes and on the spot assigned the generals to attack Baibao.

sentences.zh: 夜漏未盡，抵城下，四面合擊。

translations.literal: Before the night watch had ended they reached the city wall and attacked from all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Before the night watch had ended they reached the walls and attacked from all sides.

sentences.zh: 平明，破其城，縱兵大掠，焚巢穴，獲牛馬、橐駝七千有餘，委聚方四十里，平骨咩等四十一族。

translations.literal: At daybreak they stormed the city, let the troops plunder freely, burned the lairs, and took more than seven thousand cattle, horses, and camels; booty piled over forty li square; they pacified forty-one tribes including Pinggumie.
translations.idiomatic: At daybreak they took the city, let the troops plunder freely, burned the encampments, and captured more than seven thousand cattle, horses, and camels; the booty covered forty square li, and they pacified forty-one tribes including Pinggumie.

sentences.zh: 以功拜龍神衛四廂都指揮使、賀州防禦使，改侍衛馬軍都虞候。

translations.literal: For merit he was made commander of all four wings of the Dragon Divine Guard and defense commissioner of He Prefecture, then changed to chief adjutant of the Palace Cavalry Guard.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was made commander of all four wings of the Dragon Divine Guard and defense commissioner of Hezhou, then chief adjutant of the Palace Cavalry Guard.

sentences.zh: 康定二年春，朝廷欲發涇原、鄜延兩路兵西討，詔福詣涇原計事。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of Kangding the court wished to send troops of the Jingyuan and Fuyan circuits on a western campaign and ordered Fu to Jingyuan to plan the affair.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year of Kangding (1041) the court planned a western campaign with troops from the Jingyuan and Fuyan circuits and ordered Fu to Jingyuan to plan it.

sentences.zh: 會安撫副使韓琦行邊趨涇原，聞元昊謀寇渭州，琦亟趨鎮戎軍，盡出其兵，又募敢勇得萬八千人，使福將之。

translations.literal: Pacification deputy commissioner Han Qi was touring the frontier and hastened to Jingyuan; hearing Yuan Hao planned to raid Wei Prefecture, Qi hurried to Zhenrong army, sent out all its troops, and also recruited the daring and brave to eighteen thousand, putting Fu in command.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification deputy commissioner Han Qi was on the frontier and hurried to Jingyuan; learning that Yuan Hao planned to raid Weizhou, Qi rushed to Zhenrong, committed all its troops, and recruited eighteen thousand bold fighters, placing Fu in command.

sentences.zh: 以耿傅參軍事，涇原路駐泊都監桑懌為先鋒，鈐轄朱觀、都監武英、涇州都監王珪各以所部從福節制。

translations.literal: Geng Fu was made staff officer; Sang Yi, garrison commander of Jingyuan, was vanguard; superintendents Zhu Guan and Wu Ying and Jingzhou garrison commander Wang Gui each brought their detachments under Fu's command.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Fu served on his staff; Sang Yi, garrison commander on the Jingyuan circuit, was vanguard; Zhu Guan, Wu Ying, and Jingzhou commander Wang Gui each brought their detachments under Fu's command.

sentences.zh: 琦戒福等倂兵，自懷遠城趨得勝砦，至羊牧隆城，出敵之後。

translations.literal: Qi warned Fu and the others to unite their forces, march from Huaiyuan city toward Desheng stockade and to Yangmulong city, and take the enemy from behind.
translations.idiomatic: Qi instructed Fu and the others to unite, march from Huaiyuan toward Desheng stockade and Yangmulong, and take the enemy from behind.

sentences.zh: 諸砦相距才四十里，道近糧餉便，度勢未可戰，則據險設伏，待其歸邀擊之。

translations.literal: The stockades were only forty li apart, the roads short and supplies convenient; if he judged battle inadvisable, he should hold the passes and set ambushes, waiting for their return to strike.
translations.idiomatic: The stockades were only forty li apart and supplies easy to move; if battle seemed unwise, they should hold the passes, set ambushes, and strike the enemy on their return.

sentences.zh: 福引輕騎數千，趨懷遠城捺龍川，遇鎮戎軍西路巡檢常鼎、劉肅，與敵戰於張家堡南，斬首數百。

translations.literal: Fu led several thousand light cavalry toward Nalong Stream below Huaiyuan city, met western-route inspectors Chang Ding and Liu Su of Zhenrong army, and fought the enemy south of Zhangjiabao, beheading several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fu led several thousand light cavalry toward Nalong Stream below Huaiyuan, joined western-route inspectors Chang Ding and Liu Su of Zhenrong, and fought south of Zhangjiabao, taking several hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 夏人棄馬羊橐駝佯北，懌引騎趨之，福踵其後。

translations.literal: The Xia abandoned horses, sheep, and camels and feigned a northward retreat; Yi led cavalry in pursuit and Fu followed after.
translations.idiomatic: The Xia abandoned horses, sheep, and camels and feigned retreat; Yi led the cavalry in pursuit and Fu followed.

sentences.zh: 諜傳敵兵少，福等頗易之。

translations.literal: Spies reported the enemy few; Fu and the others took them rather lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Spies reported few enemy troops, and Fu and his officers took them lightly.

sentences.zh: 薄暮，與懌合軍屯好水川，觀、英屯龍落川，相距隔山五里，約翌日會兵川口。

translations.literal: At dusk he joined Yi and encamped at Haoshui Stream; Guan and Ying encamped at Longluo Stream, five li apart across a mountain, agreeing to unite at the stream mouth the next day.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he joined Yi and camped at Haoshui Stream; Guan and Ying camped at Longluo Stream, five li apart across a ridge, agreeing to unite at the stream mouth the next day.

sentences.zh: 路既遠，芻餉不繼，士馬乏食已三日。

translations.literal: The road was long and fodder did not keep up; men and horses had lacked food for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The road was long, fodder did not keep up, and men and horses had gone without food for three days.

sentences.zh: 追奔至籠竿城北，遇夏軍，循川行，出六盤山下，距羊牧隆城五里結陣，諸將方知墮敵計，勢不可留，遂前格戰。

translations.literal: Pursuing the flight to north of Longgan city they met Xia troops, followed the stream, came out below Liupan Mountain, and formed ranks five li from Yangmulong city; the generals then knew they had fallen into the enemy's plan; the situation could not be held, and they advanced to grapple.
translations.idiomatic: Pursuing as far as north of Longgan they met Xia forces, followed the stream, emerged below Liupan Mountain, and formed ranks five li from Yangmulong; the generals then saw they had walked into a trap and, unable to hold back, advanced to fight.

sentences.zh: 懌馳犯其鋒，福陣未成列，賊縱鐵騎突之，自辰至午，陣動，眾傅山欲據勝地。

translations.literal: Yi charged their front; Fu's formation was not yet complete when the bandits sent iron cavalry to burst upon them; from the fifth to the seventh watch the formation wavered and the masses pressed the mountain seeking advantageous ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yi charged the enemy van; Fu's ranks were not yet formed when iron cavalry burst upon them; from mid-morning to noon the line wavered and the troops pressed up the slope for better ground.

sentences.zh: 俄伏發，自山背下擊，士卒多墜崖塹，相覆壓，懌、肅戰死。

translations.literal: Soon ambush troops sprang up and struck from behind the mountain; many soldiers fell into cliffs and ditches, crushing one another; Yi and Su died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Soon ambushers struck from behind the ridge; many soldiers fell into cliffs and ravines and were crushed together; Yi and Su were killed.

sentences.zh: 敵分兵數千，斷官軍後，福力戰，身被十餘矢。

translations.literal: The enemy divided several thousand men to cut off the government army's rear; Fu fought hard and was struck by more than ten arrows.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy sent several thousand men to cut off the army's rear; Fu fought on and was struck by more than ten arrows.

sentences.zh: 有小校劉進者，勸福自免。

translations.literal: A petty officer named Liu Jin urged Fu to save himself.
translations.idiomatic: A petty officer named Liu Jin urged Fu to save himself.

sentences.zh: 福曰：「吾為大將，兵敗，以死報國爾。

translations.literal: Fu said: "I am the great general; the army is defeated—I repay the state with death, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Fu said, "I am the commander; the army is beaten—I repay the state with my death, nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」揮四刃鐵簡，挺身決鬥，槍中左頰，絕其喉而死。

translations.literal: " He swung a four-edged iron mace, threw himself into decisive combat, was struck in the left cheek by a spear, and his throat was severed—he died.
translations.idiomatic: He swung a four-edged iron mace and fought to the death; a spear struck his left cheek and severed his throat.

sentences.zh: 乃倂兵攻觀、英。

translations.literal: The enemy then united forces to attack Guan and Ying.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy then turned their combined force on Guan and Ying.

sentences.zh: 戰既合，王珪自羊牧隆城引兵四千，陣於觀軍之西；

translations.literal: When battle was joined, Wang Gui from Yangmulong city led four thousand troops and formed ranks west of Guan's force;
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined, Wang Gui led four thousand men from Yangmulong and formed ranks west of Guan's force;

sentences.zh: 渭州駐泊都監趙津將瓦亭騎兵二千繼至。

translations.literal: Zhao Jin, garrison commander of Wei Prefecture, brought two thousand Wating cavalry in support.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Jin, garrison commander of Weizhou, brought two thousand Wating cavalry in support.

sentences.zh: 珪屢出略陣，陣堅不可破，英重傷，不能視軍。

translations.literal: Gui repeatedly sallied to probe the formation, but it was firm and could not be broken; Ying was gravely wounded and could not command the army.
translations.idiomatic: Gui repeatedly probed the enemy line but could not break it; Ying was gravely wounded and unable to command.

sentences.zh: 敵兵益至，官軍遂大潰，英、津、珪、傅皆死；

translations.literal: Enemy troops increased; the government army then collapsed utterly; Ying, Jin, Gui, and Fu all died;
translations.idiomatic: More enemy troops arrived and the government army broke completely; Ying, Jin, Gui, and Fu were all killed;

sentences.zh: 內殿崇班訾贇、西頭供奉官王慶、侍禁李簡、李禹亨、劉鈞亦戰沒；

translations.literal: Inner Palace Attendant Zi Yun, western palace supply officer Wang Qing, and palace guards Li Jian, Li Yuheng, and Liu Jun also fell in battle;
translations.idiomatic: Zi Yun, Wang Qing, and palace guards Li Jian, Li Yuheng, and Liu Jun also fell in battle;

sentences.zh: 軍校死者數十人，士死者六千餘人。

translations.literal: several tens of officers died and more than six thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: several dozen officers and more than six thousand soldiers were killed.

sentences.zh: 唯觀以兵千餘保民垣，四嚮縱射，會暮，敵引去，與福戰處相距五里，然其敗不相聞也。

translations.literal: Only Guan with a little more than a thousand men held a civilian wall, shooting in all four directions; at dusk the enemy withdrew; he was five li from where Fu fought, yet did not hear of the defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Only Guan, with a little more than a thousand men, held a village wall and shot in all directions; at dusk the enemy withdrew. He was five li from where Fu fought, yet heard nothing of the defeat.

sentences.zh: 福子懷亮亦死之。

translations.literal: Fu's son Huailiang also died.
translations.idiomatic: Fu's son Huailiang also died.

sentences.zh: 方元昊傾國入寇，福臨敵受命，所統皆非素撫之兵，既又分出趨利，故至於甚敗。

translations.literal: Just as Yuan Hao threw the whole state into invasion, Fu took command facing the enemy; those he led were none troops he had long commanded, and they had moreover been split apart to chase gain—thus the great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao had thrown his whole state into the invasion; Fu took command facing an enemy with troops he had not long commanded, and they had been split apart in pursuit of booty—hence the great defeat.

sentences.zh: 奏至，帝震悼，贈福武勝軍節度使兼侍中，賜第一區，月給其家錢三萬，粟、麥四十斛。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived the emperor was shaken with grief; Fu was posthumously made military governor of the Wusheng army and concurrent palace attendant, granted one mansion, and his household given thirty thousand cash monthly and forty hu of grain and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: When the report reached court the emperor was stricken with grief; Fu was posthumously made military governor of the Wusheng army and concurrent palace attendant, granted a mansion, and his family given thirty thousand cash a month and forty hu of grain and wheat.

sentences.zh: 追封母為隴西郡太夫人，妻為琅琊郡夫人，錄其子及從子凡六人。

translations.literal: His mother was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Lady of Longxi commandery, his wife as Lady of Langya commandery, and his sons and nephews, six in all, were enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was posthumously made Grand Lady of Longxi commandery and his wife Lady of Langya commandery; his sons and nephews, six in all, were enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 王珪

translations.literal: Wang Gui
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui

translations.literal: (Appended biography)
translations.idiomatic: (Appended biography)

sentences.zh: 王珪，開封人也。

translations.literal: Wang Gui was a man of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui was from Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 少拳勇，善騎射，能用鐵杵、鐵鞭。

translations.literal: In youth he was bold in boxing, skilled in riding and archery, and could wield iron mace and iron whip.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he was bold and skilled at riding and archery, and could wield an iron mace and iron whip.

sentences.zh: 年十九，隸親從官，累遷殿前第一班押班，擢禮賓副使、涇州駐泊都監。

translations.literal: At nineteen he entered the personal attendants, was repeatedly promoted to escort commander of the Palace Front first rank, and advanced to deputy commissioner of ceremonial guests and Jingzhou garrison commander.
translations.idiomatic: At nineteen he entered the personal attendants, rose to escort commander of the Palace Front first rank, and was made deputy commissioner of ceremonial guests and garrison commander of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 康定初，元昊寇鎮戎軍，珪將三千騎為策先鋒，自瓦亭至師子堡，敵圍之數重，

translations.literal: Early in Kangding, when Yuan Hao raided Zhenrong army, Gui led three thousand cavalry as raiding vanguard from Wating to Shizi fort; the enemy surrounded them in many rings,
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kangding, when Yuan Hao raided Zhenrong, Gui led three thousand cavalry as raiding vanguard from Wating to Shizi fort, where the enemy surrounded them in layer after layer,

sentences.zh: 珪奮擊披靡，獲首級為多。

translations.literal: Gui fought fiercely and swept all before him, taking the most heads.
translations.idiomatic: Gui fought fiercely and swept the enemy aside, taking more heads than any other.

sentences.zh: 叩鎮戎城，請益兵，不許。

translations.literal: He knocked at Zhenrong city and asked for more troops; it was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Zhenrong and asked for reinforcements, but none were sent.

sentences.zh: 城中惟縋糗糧予之。

translations.literal: The city only lowered dry rations to him.
translations.idiomatic: The city could only lower dry rations down to him on ropes.

sentences.zh: 師既飽，因語其下曰：「兵法，以寡擊眾必在暮，我兵少，乘其暮擊之，可得志也。

translations.literal: When the troops were fed, he told his men: "In military law, to strike many with few one must do it at dusk; our troops are few—strike them at dusk and we can succeed."
translations.idiomatic: When his men had eaten, he told them, "By the art of war, the few must strike the many at dusk; we are few—hit them at dusk and we can prevail."

sentences.zh: 」 復馳入，有驍將持白幟植槍以詈曰：「誰敢與吾敵者！

translations.literal: " He charged in again; a fierce general held a white banner, planted his spear, and cursed: "Who dares be my enemy!"
translations.idiomatic: He charged in again. A fierce champion planted his spear with a white banner and shouted, "Who dares face me!"

sentences.zh: 」槍直珪胸而傷右臂，珪左手以杵碎其腦。

translations.literal: " The spear pierced Gui's chest and wounded his right arm; with his left hand Gui shattered his skull with the mace.
translations.idiomatic: The spear struck Gui's chest and wounded his right arm; with his left hand he shattered the man's skull with his mace.

sentences.zh: 繼又一將復以槍進，珪挾其槍，以鞭擊殺之。

translations.literal: Then another general again advanced with a spear; Gui seized the spear and killed him with his whip.
translations.idiomatic: Another officer advanced with a spear; Gui seized the spear and killed him with his whip.

sentences.zh: 一軍大驚，遂引去。

translations.literal: The whole army was greatly alarmed and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The whole enemy army was shaken and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 珪亦以馬中箭而還，仁宗特遣使撫諭之；

translations.literal: Gui also returned with his horse struck by arrows; Renzong specially sent envoys to comfort and instruct him;
translations.idiomatic: Gui also returned with his horse wounded by arrows; Emperor Renzong specially sent envoys to comfort him;

sentences.zh: 然以其下死傷亦多，止賜名馬二匹，黃金三十兩，裹創絹百匹；

translations.literal: yet because his subordinates' dead and wounded were also many, he was only given two famous horses, thirty liang of gold, and a hundred bolts of silk for dressing wounds;
translations.idiomatic: but because his men had also suffered heavy casualties, he received only two fine horses, thirty liang of gold, and a hundred bolts of silk for dressing wounds;

sentences.zh: 復下詔暴其功塞下，以厲諸將。

translations.literal: an edict was again issued proclaiming his merit on the frontier to encourage the generals.
translations.idiomatic: and an edict proclaimed his merit on the frontier to encourage the other generals.

sentences.zh: 是歲，改涇原路都監。

translations.literal: That year he was changed to overall garrison commander of the Jingyuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: That year he was made overall garrison commander on the Jingyuan circuit.

sentences.zh: 明年，為本路行營都臨，勒金字處置牌賜之，使得專誅殺。

translations.literal: The next year he was made overall overseer of the circuit field camp; a gold-inscribed disposition tablet was bestowed on him, granting exclusive power of execution.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made overall overseer of the circuit field camp and granted a gold-inscribed disposition tablet with exclusive power of execution.

sentences.zh: 尋至黑山，焚敵族帳，獲首級、馬駝甚眾。

translations.literal: Shortly he reached Black Mountain, burned enemy tribal tents, and took very many heads, horses, and camels.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he reached Black Mountain, burned enemy encampments, and took a great many heads, horses, and camels.

sentences.zh: 會敵大入，以兵五千從任福屯好水川，連戰三日，諸將皆敗。

translations.literal: When the enemy invaded in force, with five thousand troops he followed Ren Fu and encamped at Haoshui Stream; fighting continued three days and all the generals were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy invaded in force he followed Ren Fu with five thousand men to Haoshui Stream; after three days of fighting all the generals were beaten.

sentences.zh: 任福陷圍中，望見麾幟猶在，珪欲援出之，軍校有顧望不進者，斬以徇。

translations.literal: Ren Fu was trapped in the encirclement; seeing the command banners still there, Gui wished to rescue him; an officer who hesitated and would not advance was beheaded to warn the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Fu was trapped in the encirclement; when Gui saw his command banners still flying he tried to rescue him, and beheaded an officer who hung back as a warning to the rest.

sentences.zh: 乃東望再拜曰：「非臣負國，臣力不能也，獨有死報爾。

translations.literal: He then bowed twice toward the east and said: "It is not that your servant has failed the state—your servant's strength cannot do more; I have only death to repay it."
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice toward the east and said, "I have not failed the state—my strength is spent; I have only my death left to offer."

sentences.zh: 」乃復入戰，殺數十百人，鞭鐵撓曲，手掌盡裂，奮擊自若。

translations.literal: " He then reentered battle, killed several tens or hundreds, his iron whip bent, his palms all split, yet fought on as before.
translations.idiomatic: He went back into the fight, killed scores of the enemy, bent his iron whip, split both palms, and still fought on without faltering.

sentences.zh: 馬中鏃，凡三易，猶馳擊殺數十人。

translations.literal: His horse was struck by arrows; he changed horses three times in all, yet still galloped and killed several tens.
translations.idiomatic: His horse was hit by arrows; he changed mounts three times and still killed dozens more in the charge.

sentences.zh: 矢中目，乃還，夜中卒。

translations.literal: An arrow struck his eye; he then withdrew and died in the night.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow struck his eye; he withdrew and died that night.

sentences.zh: 珪少通陰陽術數之學，始出戰，謂其家人曰：「我前後大小二十餘戰，殺敵多矣，今恐不得還。

translations.literal: Gui in youth understood yin-yang and numerology; as he set out for battle he told his family: "I have fought more than twenty engagements large and small and killed many enemies; now I fear I shall not return."
translations.idiomatic: Gui had studied yin-yang lore and divination in youth; as he set out for battle he told his family, "I have fought more than twenty engagements and killed many enemies; I fear I shall not return this time."

sentences.zh: 我死，可速去此，無為敵所仇也。

translations.literal: When I die, leave this place quickly and do not let the enemy take revenge on you."
translations.idiomatic: When I die, leave this place quickly so the enemy cannot take revenge on you."

sentences.zh: 」及敵攻瓦亭，購甚急，果如所料。

translations.literal: When the enemy attacked Wating the price on their heads was very urgent, just as he had foreseen.
translations.idiomatic: When the enemy attacked Wating the bounty on his family was posted at once, just as he had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 鎮戎之戰，以所得二槍植山上，其後邊人即其處為立祠。

translations.literal: In the battle at Zhenrong he planted the two spears he had taken on the mountain; later frontier people erected a shrine on that spot.
translations.idiomatic: After the battle at Zhenrong he planted the two spears he had captured on a hill, and later the frontier people built a shrine there.

sentences.zh: 贈金州觀察使，追封其妻安康郡君，錄其子光祖為西頭供奉官、閤門祗候，後為東上閤門使；

translations.literal: He was posthumously made surveillance commissioner of Jin Prefecture; his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Ankang commandery; his son Guangzu was enrolled as western palace supply officer and palace gate attendant, later eastern upper palace gate attendant;
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made surveillance commissioner of Jinzhou; his wife was enfeoffed as Lady of Ankang commandery; his son Guangzu was enrolled as western palace supply officer and palace gate attendant, later eastern upper palace gate attendant;

sentences.zh: 光世，西頭供奉官；

translations.literal: Guangshi, western palace supply officer;
translations.idiomatic: Guangshi, western palace supply officer;

sentences.zh: 光嗣，左侍禁。

translations.literal: Guangsi, left palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Guangsi, left palace guard.

sentences.zh: 武英

translations.literal: Wu Ying
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ying

translations.literal: 〈Appended biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 武英，字漢傑，太原人。

translations.literal: Wu Ying, styled Hanjie, was a man of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Ying, whose courtesy name was Hanjie, was from Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 父密，隨劉繼元歸朝，仕至侍禁、鎮定同巡檢。

translations.literal: His father Mi followed Liu Jiyuan in submission to the court and served up to palace guard and concurrent inspector of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: His father Mi had followed Liu Jiyuan in submitting to the Song and rose to palace guard and concurrent inspector of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 與契丹戰，沒於望都，贈西京左坊使，錄英為三班借職，以右班殿直為忻、代州同巡檢。

translations.literal: Fighting the Khitan he perished at Wangdu; posthumously made western capital left ward keeper; Ying was enrolled as borrowed third-rank attendant and made right-rank palace attendant and concurrent inspector of Xin and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He died fighting the Khitan at Wangdu and was posthumously made western capital left ward keeper; Ying was enrolled as borrowed third-rank attendant and made right-rank palace attendant and concurrent inspector of Xin and Dai.

sentences.zh: 會州將出獵，因留帳飲，英曰：「今空郡而來，萬一敵乘間入城，奈何？

translations.literal: The prefect of Hui Prefecture was going out to hunt and stayed in the tent to drink; Ying said: "You have come with the prefecture empty—if by chance the enemy slips into the city, what then?"
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Huizhou was going hunting and stayed in camp to drink; Ying said, "You have left the prefecture empty—what if the enemy slips into the city?"

sentences.zh: 」既而敵百餘騎果入寇，英領眾左右馳射，悉禽獲之。

translations.literal: " Before long more than a hundred enemy horsemen did raid in; Ying led the troops shooting left and right in gallop and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: Before long more than a hundred enemy horsemen did raid in; Ying led his men in a galloping fight and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 以功遷左班殿直、監雄州榷場，改右侍禁、閤門祗候，為環州都巡檢使，徙洪德砦主，又徙慶州柔遠砦。
