translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to left-rank palace attendant and supervisor of the Xiongzhou trade office, changed to right palace guard and palace gate attendant, made overall inspector of Huan Prefecture, transferred to master of Hongde stockade, and again to Rouyuan stockade in Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was promoted to left-rank palace attendant and supervisor of the Xiongzhou trade office, then made right palace guard and palace gate attendant, overall inspector of Huanzhou, commander of Hongde stockade, and finally Rouyuan stockade in Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇延州，英主兵攻後橋，以分敵勢。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao raided Yan Prefecture, Ying commanded troops to attack Houqiao and divide the enemy's strength.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao raided Yanzhou, Ying led troops against Houqiao to divide the enemy's strength.

sentences.zh: 擢內殿承制、環慶路駐泊都監。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Inner Palace Commissioner and garrison commander of the Huanqing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to inner palace commissioner and garrison commander on the Huanqing circuit.

sentences.zh: 破黨平族，又從任福破白豹城，遷禮賓副使，尋兼涇原行營都監。

translations.literal: He defeated the Dangping tribe, followed Ren Fu in storming Baibao city, was promoted to deputy commissioner of ceremonial guests, and soon also served as overall overseer of the Jingyuan field camp.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated the Dangping tribe, followed Ren Fu in taking Baibao, was made deputy commissioner of ceremonial guests, and soon also oversaw the Jingyuan field camp.

sentences.zh: 與任福合諸將戰張家堡，斬首數十百，敵棄羊馬偽遁。

translations.literal: With Ren Fu he united the generals in battle at Zhangjiabao, beheading several tens or hundreds; the enemy abandoned sheep and horses and feigned flight.
translations.idiomatic: With Ren Fu he united the generals at Zhangjiabao and took several tens or hundreds of heads; the enemy abandoned sheep and horses and feigned retreat.

sentences.zh: 諸將皆趨利爭進，英以為前必有伏，眾不聽，已而伏發。

translations.literal: All the generals rushed for gain and vied to advance; Ying thought ambush lay ahead; the host would not listen, and soon the ambush sprang.
translations.idiomatic: The generals all rushed forward for booty; Ying warned that an ambush lay ahead, but they would not listen, and soon the trap was sprung.

sentences.zh: 福等既敗，英猶力戰，自辰至申，矢盡遇害。

translations.literal: After Fu and the others were defeated, Ying still fought hard from the fifth to the ninth watch until his arrows were spent and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: After Fu's defeat Ying still fought from mid-morning to mid-afternoon until his arrows were spent and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈邢州觀察使。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made surveillance commissioner of Xing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made surveillance commissioner of Xingzhou.

sentences.zh: 錄其子三班奉職永符為東頭供奉官、閤門祗候；

translations.literal: His son Yongfu, third-rank attendant, was enrolled as eastern palace supply officer and palace gate attendant;
translations.idiomatic: His son Yongfu, a third-rank attendant, was enrolled as eastern palace supply officer and palace gate attendant;

sentences.zh: 永孚，西頭供奉官；

translations.literal: Yongfu, western palace supply officer;
translations.idiomatic: Yongfu, western palace supply officer;

sentences.zh: 永昌，左侍禁。

translations.literal: Yongchang, left palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yongchang, left palace guard.

sentences.zh: 侄永保，右班殿直；

translations.literal: Nephew Yongbao, right-hand palace guard attendant;
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Yongbao was made a right-hand palace guard attendant;

sentences.zh: 永錫，三班奉職。

translations.literal: Yongxi, third-rank attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi, third-rank attendant.

sentences.zh: 桑懌

translations.literal: Sang Yi
translations.idiomatic: Sang Yi

translations.literal: 〈Appended biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 桑懌，開封雍丘人。

translations.literal: Sang Yi was a native of Yongqiu in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Sang Yi was from Yongqiu in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 勇力過人，善用劍及鐵簡，有謀略。

translations.literal: His courage and strength surpassed others; he was skilled with the sword and iron mace; he had stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: Exceptionally brave and strong, skilled with sword and iron mace, and gifted with strategy.

sentences.zh: 其為人不甚長大，與人接，常祗畏若不自足，語言如不出其口，卒遇之，不知其勇且健也。

translations.literal: He was not very tall; in meeting others he was always deferential as if insufficient; his words seemed barely to leave his mouth; on sudden encounter one would not know his courage and vigor.
translations.idiomatic: He was not tall, and in company he was so deferential one might think him timid; his speech seemed barely to leave his lips; a stranger would never guess how brave and fit he was.

sentences.zh: 兄慥，舉進士，有名。

translations.literal: His elder brother Cao passed the jinshi examination and was famed.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Cao had passed the jinshi examination and won renown.

sentences.zh: 懌以再舉進士，不中。

translations.literal: Yi twice took the jinshi examination and failed.
translations.idiomatic: Yi twice sat for the jinshi examination and failed both times.

sentences.zh: 嘗遭大水，有粟二廩，將以舟載之，見百姓走避水者，遂棄其粟而載之，得皆不死。

translations.literal: Once during a great flood he had grain in two granaries and was about to load it by boat; seeing common people fleeing the water, he abandoned his grain and carried them instead, so that all escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: Once during a great flood he had grain in two granaries and meant to ferry it away, but when he saw people fleeing the water he abandoned the grain and took them aboard instead, and all were saved.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，聚人共食其粟，盡而止。

translations.literal: In a famine year he gathered people to eat his grain together, and stopped when it was gone.
translations.idiomatic: In a year of famine he gathered people to share his grain until it was all gone.

sentences.zh: 後徙居汝、潁間，耕龍城廢田數頃以自給。

translations.literal: Later he moved to live between Ru and Ying, farming several qing of abandoned fields at Longcheng to support himself.
translations.idiomatic: Later he moved to the region between Ru and Ying and farmed several qing of abandoned fields at Longcheng to support himself.

sentences.zh: 諸縣多盜，懌自請補耆長，得往來察奸，因召里中惡少年戒曰：「盜不可為，吾不汝容也。

translations.literal: Many counties had bandits; Yi volunteered to fill the post of elder chief, was able to go about investigating wrongdoing, and summoned the wicked youths of the lane to warn them: "Robbery must not be done—I will not tolerate you."
translations.idiomatic: Banditry was rife in the counties; Yi volunteered as elder chief so he could investigate crime, and summoned the neighborhood's bad youths to warn them, "Do not turn to robbery—I will not spare you."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，里老父子死未斂，盜夜脫其衣去，父不敢告縣。

translations.literal: " Before long an old man of the lane and his son died and lay unburied; a bandit stripped their clothes by night and left; the father dared not report it to the county.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an old man and his son in the lane died and lay unburied; a thief stripped their shrouds one night, and the father dared not report it to the magistrate.

sentences.zh: 懌疑少年王生者，夜入其家，得其衣，不使之知也。

translations.literal: Yi suspected a youth surnamed Wang; he entered his house by night, obtained the clothes, and did not let him know.
translations.idiomatic: Yi suspected a youth named Wang; he entered the house at night, recovered the clothes, and kept Wang from knowing.

sentences.zh: 明日，見而問之曰：「爾許我不為盜，今里中盜屍衣者，非爾邪？

translations.literal: The next day he saw him and asked: "You promised me you would not rob—now the one in the lane who robbed the corpse's clothes, is it not you?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he confronted him and asked, "You promised me you would not steal—so was it you who robbed the dead in our lane?"

sentences.zh: 」少年色動，即推仆地，縛之，詰共盜者姓名，盡送縣，皆伏辜。

translations.literal: " The youth's face changed; Yi at once pushed him down, bound him, questioned the names of his fellow robbers, sent them all to the county, and all confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The youth's face changed; Yi threw him down, bound him, extracted the names of his accomplices, sent them all to the county, and every one confessed.

sentences.zh: 嘗之郟城，遇尉出捕盜，招懌飲酒。

translations.literal: Once he went to Yancheng and met the district captain going out to catch bandits, who invited Yi to drink.
translations.idiomatic: Once in Yancheng he met the district captain setting out to catch bandits, who invited him to drink.

sentences.zh: 與俱行，至賊所藏，尉怯甚，陽為不知，將去。

translations.literal: They went together; when they reached where the bandits hid, the captain was very afraid, pretended not to know, and was about to leave.
translations.idiomatic: They went together; when they reached the bandits' hiding place the captain was so afraid he pretended not to see them and was about to turn back.

sentences.zh: 懌曰：「賊在此，欲何之？

translations.literal: Yi said: "The bandits are here—where do you mean to go?"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The bandits are right here—where are you going?"

sentences.zh: 」乃下馬，獨格殺數人，因盡縛之。

translations.literal: " He then dismounted, alone killed several in combat, and bound them all.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted, killed several in hand-to-hand combat by himself, and bound the rest.

sentences.zh: 又聞襄城有盜十許人，獨提一劍以往，殺數人，盡縛其餘，汝旁縣為之無盜。

translations.literal: Again he heard Xiangcheng had some ten bandits; alone bearing one sword he went, killed several, bound the rest entirely, and the counties beside Ru were thereby without bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Xiangcheng had some ten bandits, he went alone with a single sword, killed several, bound the rest, and the counties around Ru were rid of banditry.

sentences.zh: 京西轉運使奏其事，補郟城尉。

translations.literal: The Jingxi transport commissioner reported the matter, and he was appointed district captain of Yancheng.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingxi transport commissioner reported his deeds, and he was appointed district captain of Yancheng.

sentences.zh: 天聖中，河南諸縣多盜，轉運使奏移澠池尉。

translations.literal: In the Tiansheng era many counties in Henan had bandits; the transport commissioner memorialized to transfer him as district captain of Mianchi.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tiansheng era banditry was rife in Henan counties, and the transport commissioner had him transferred to serve as district captain of Mianchi.

sentences.zh: 群盜保青灰山，時出攘剽。

translations.literal: A band of robbers held Qinghui Mountain and from time to time came out to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: A band of robbers held Qinghui Mountain and raided the countryside from time to time.

sentences.zh: 有宿盜王伯者，尤為民害，朝廷每授巡檢使，必疏姓名使捕之。

translations.literal: There was a veteran bandit Wang Bo who was especially a harm to the people; whenever the court appointed an inspection commissioner, it always listed names and ordered his capture.
translations.idiomatic: A veteran bandit named Wang Bo was especially feared; whenever the court appointed an inspection commissioner, Wang's name was always listed for capture.

sentences.zh: 懌至官，巡檢偽為宣頭以示懌，牒招致之。

translations.literal: When Yi took office, the inspection commissioner forged an imperial order to show Yi and by dispatch summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi took office, the inspection commissioner forged an imperial order to show him and summoned him by dispatch.

sentences.zh: 懌不知其偽也，因挺身入賊中，與伯同臥起，十餘日，伯遂與懌出至山口，為巡檢伏兵所執，懌幾不免。

translations.literal: Yi did not know it was forged; he therefore entered the bandits' midst, rose and lay down with Bo for more than ten days; Bo then went out with Yi to the mountain pass, where inspection commissioner ambush troops seized him; Yi nearly did not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Not knowing the order was forged, Yi entered the bandits' camp and lived with Bo for more than ten days; when Bo led him out to the pass, the inspector's ambush seized Bo, and Yi nearly died in the trap.

sentences.zh: 懌曰：「巡檢懼無功爾。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The inspection commissioner feared having no merit—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The inspector only feared coming away with no credit."

sentences.zh: 」即以伯與巡檢，使自為功。

translations.literal: " He then gave Bo to the inspection commissioner and let him claim the merit himself.
translations.idiomatic: He handed Wang Bo over to the inspector and let him claim the credit.

sentences.zh: 巡檢俘獻京師，而懌不復自言。

translations.literal: The inspection commissioner presented the captive in the capital, while Yi did not speak of himself again.
translations.idiomatic: The inspector presented the captive in the capital, but Yi never spoke of his own part.

sentences.zh: 朝廷知之，為黜巡檢，擢懌右班殿直、永安縣巡檢。

translations.literal: The court learned of it, demoted the inspection commissioner for it, and promoted Yi to right-hand palace guard attendant and Yong'an county inspector.
translations.idiomatic: When the court learned what had happened, it demoted the inspector and promoted Yi to right-hand palace guard attendant and inspector of Yong'an County.

sentences.zh: 明道末，京西旱蝗，有惡賊二十三人，樞密院召懌至京師，授以賊名姓，使往捕。

translations.literal: At the end of the Mingdao era Jingxi suffered drought and locusts; there were twenty-three vicious bandits; the Bureau of Military Affairs summoned Yi to the capital, gave him the bandits' names, and sent him to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Mingdao era drought and locusts struck Jingxi, and twenty-three vicious bandits were at large; the Bureau of Military Affairs summoned Yi to the capital, gave him their names, and sent him to capture them.

sentences.zh: 懌曰：「盜畏吾名，必潰，潰則難得矣，宜先示之以怯。

translations.literal: Yi said: "The bandits fear my name and will surely scatter; once scattered they are hard to catch—we should first show them timidity."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "The bandits fear my name and will scatter; once scattered they are hard to catch. We should first make them think us timid."

sentences.zh: 」至則閉柵，戒軍吏不得一人輒出。

translations.literal: " On arrival he closed the stockade and warned the military clerks that not one man might go out on his own.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he shut the camp gates and ordered that not a single soldier was to leave.

sentences.zh: 居數日，軍吏不知所為，數請出自效，輒不許。

translations.literal: After several days the military clerks did not know what to do and repeatedly asked to go out and prove themselves, but he always refused.
translations.idiomatic: After several days the officers did not know what he intended and repeatedly asked permission to go out and fight, but he always refused.

sentences.zh: 夜，與數卒變為盜服以出，跡盜所嘗行處。

translations.literal: At night he and several soldiers changed into bandit dress and went out, tracking where the bandits had walked.
translations.idiomatic: One night he and several soldiers dressed as bandits and went out to trace the routes they used.

sentences.zh: 入民家，民皆走，獨一媼留，為具飲食，如事群盜。

translations.literal: They entered a commoner's house; the people all fled; only one old woman remained and prepared food and drink for them as if serving a band of robbers.
translations.idiomatic: They entered a farmhouse; everyone fled except one old woman, who prepared food and drink for them as if they were real bandits.

sentences.zh: 懌歸，閉柵三日，復往，自攜具就媼饌，而以餘遺媼，媼以為真盜。

translations.literal: Yi returned, closed the stockade three days, then went again, himself carrying provisions to dine with the old woman and leaving the remainder to her; the old woman took them for real bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Yi returned and kept the camp shut for three days, then went back with provisions, ate with the old woman, and left her the leftovers; she took them for genuine bandits.

sentences.zh: 乃稍就媼，與語及群盜，一媼曰：「彼聞桑殿直來，皆遁去。

translations.literal: He then drew somewhat near the old woman and spoke with her of the band of robbers; one old woman said: "When they heard Palace Attendant Sang was coming, they all fled."
translations.idiomatic: He drew the old woman into talk about the bandits, and she said, "When they heard Palace Attendant Sang was coming, they all fled."

sentences.zh: 近聞閉營不出，知其不足畏，今皆還矣，某在某處。

translations.literal: Lately hearing the camp was shut and no one came out, they knew he was not to be feared; now they have all returned—so-and-so is at such-and-such a place."
translations.idiomatic: But lately they heard the camp was shut and no one came out, so they knew he was nothing to fear; now they have all come back—so-and-so is at such-and-such a place."

sentences.zh: 」懌又三日往，厚遺之，遂以實告曰：「我桑殿直也，為我察其實而慎勿泄。

translations.literal: " After three days Yi went again, gave her generous gifts, and then told her the truth: "I am Palace Attendant Sang—investigate the facts for me and be careful not to reveal it."
translations.idiomatic: Three days later Yi returned with generous gifts and told her the truth: "I am Palace Attendant Sang—investigate for me, but be careful not to betray me."

sentences.zh: 」後三日復來，於是媼盡得居處之實以告。

translations.literal: " Three days later he came again; then the old woman told him in full the truth of where they dwelt.
translations.idiomatic: Three days later he came again, and by then the old woman had learned every hideout and told him all.

sentences.zh: 懌明日部分軍士，盡擒諸盜。

translations.literal: The next day Yi deployed the soldiers in sections and captured all the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Yi deployed his troops in sections and captured every bandit.

sentences.zh: 其尤強梁者，懌自馳馬以往，士卒不及從，惟四騎追之，遂與賊遇，手殺三人。

translations.literal: Among the most violent, Yi himself galloped there; the soldiers could not keep up—only four horsemen pursued; he then met the bandits and with his own hand killed three.
translations.idiomatic: For the toughest of them Yi galloped ahead himself; his men could not keep up, and only four riders followed; he met the bandits and killed three with his own hand.

sentences.zh: 凡二十三人者，一日皆獲。

translations.literal: All twenty-three were captured in a single day.
translations.idiomatic: All twenty-three were captured in a single day.

sentences.zh: 還京師，樞密吏求銀，為致閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital, a Bureau of Military Affairs clerk asked for silver and would secure for him the post of palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital, a Bureau clerk demanded silver and offered to secure him the post of palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 懌曰：「用賂得官，非我欲，況貧無銀；

translations.literal: Yi said: "To buy office with a bribe is not what I want; moreover I am poor and have no silver;"
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "Buying an office with a bribe is not what I want, and besides I am too poor to have silver;"

sentences.zh: 有，固不可也。

translations.literal: if I had it, I surely could not do so.
translations.idiomatic: and even if I had it, I still could not do such a thing.

sentences.zh: 」吏怒，匿其功狀，止免其短使而已。

translations.literal: " The clerk was angry, concealed his merit record, and only exempted him from short-term corvée.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk was furious, suppressed his merit report, and only exempted him from short-term corvée duty.

sentences.zh: 除兵馬監押，未行，會宜州蠻叛，殺海上巡檢，官軍不能制，因命懌往，盡手殺之。

translations.literal: He was made horse and equipment supervisor; before he set out, the Yi Prefecture tribes rebelled, killed the maritime inspection commissioner, and government troops could not control them; he was therefore ordered to go, and killed them all with his own hand.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed horse and equipment supervisor, but before he could take up the post the Yi tribes of Yizhou rebelled, killed the maritime inspector, and government troops could not suppress them; Yi was sent and killed them all himself.

sentences.zh: 還，乃授閤門祗候。

translations.literal: On return he was then granted the post of palace gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was made palace gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 懌曰：「是行也，非獨吾功，位有居吾上者，吾乃其佐也。

translations.literal: Yi said: "On this expedition the merit was not mine alone—there was one whose rank stood above me; I was only his assistant."
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, "On that campaign the credit was not mine alone—there was a man above me in rank, and I was only his deputy."

sentences.zh: 今彼留而我還，我賞厚而彼輕，得不疑我蓋其功而自伐乎？

translations.literal: Now he stayed behind while I returned; my reward is thick and his slight—would he not suspect that I covered his merit and boasted of myself?"
translations.idiomatic: He stayed behind while I came home; my reward is generous and his slight—will he not suspect that I stole his credit and boasted of myself?"

sentences.zh: 受之，徒慚吾心。

translations.literal: To accept it would only shame my heart.
translations.idiomatic: To accept the post would only shame my conscience.

sentences.zh: 」將讓其賞以歸己上者。

translations.literal: " He was about to yield his reward to the one above him.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to yield his reward to his superior.

sentences.zh: 或譏以好名，懌歎曰：「士顧其心如何爾，當自信其心以行，若欲避名，則善皆不可為也。

translations.literal: Some mocked him for courting fame; Yi sighed and said: "A gentleman looks to what his heart is like—that is all; he should trust his heart and act; if one wishes to avoid fame, then no good deed can be done."
translations.idiomatic: Some mocked him for seeking fame; Yi sighed and said, "A gentleman need only heed what is in his heart and act on that faith; if you try to flee reputation, then no good deed can be done at all."

sentences.zh: 」益辭之，不許。

translations.literal: " He refused all the more, but was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He refused all the more, but was not allowed.

sentences.zh: 寶元初，遷西頭供奉官、廣西駐泊都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Baoyuan he was transferred to western palace supply officer and Guangxi garrison supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Baoyuan era he was made western palace supply officer and overall supervisor of the Guangxi garrison.

sentences.zh: 元昊反，參知政事宋庠薦其有勇略，遷內殿崇班、鄜延路兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When Yuan Hao rebelled, Vice Grand Councillor Song Qi recommended his courage and stratagem; he was transferred to inner palace honored attendant and Yan'an circuit military supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Hao rebelled, Vice Grand Councillor Song Qi recommended him for courage and strategy, and he was made inner palace honored attendant and military supervisor of the Yan'an circuit.

sentences.zh: 逾月，徙涇原路，屯鎮戎軍，與任福遇敵於好水川，力戰而死。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was moved to the Jingyuan circuit, garrisoned at Zhenrong Army, met the enemy with Ren Fu at Haoshuichuan, fought fiercely, and died.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was transferred to the Jingyuan circuit, garrisoned at Zhenrong Army, met the enemy with Ren Fu at Haoshuichuan, fought to the end, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈解州防禦使；

translations.literal: He was posthumously made defense commissioner of Jie Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made defense commissioner of Jiezhou;

sentences.zh: 子湜皇城使。

translations.literal: his son Chi was made palace envoy.
translations.idiomatic: his son Chi was made palace envoy.

sentences.zh: 耿傅

translations.literal: Geng Fu
translations.idiomatic: Geng Fu

translations.literal: 〈Appended biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 耿傅，字公弼，河南人。

translations.literal: Geng Fu, courtesy name Gongbi, was a native of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Fu, courtesy name Gongbi, was from Henan.

sentences.zh: 祖昭化，為蜀州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhaohua served as revenue registrar of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhaohua served as revenue registrar of Shuzhou.

sentences.zh: 盜據城，欲脅以官，昭化大罵，至斷手足，不屈而死。

translations.literal: Bandits seized the city and wished to coerce him with office; Zhaohua cursed them loudly, until they cut off his hands and feet, yet he did not yield and died.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits seized the city they tried to force an office on him; Zhaohua cursed them until they cut off his hands and feet, but he would not yield and died.

sentences.zh: 傅少喜俠尚氣，初以父蔭為三班奉職，換伊陽縣尉，歷明州司理參軍，遷將作監丞、知永寧縣。

translations.literal: Fu in youth loved chivalry and prized spirit; at first through his father's privilege he was made third-rank attendant, exchanged to district captain of Yiyang, passed through judicial assistant of Ming Prefecture, and was promoted to construction supervisor of the imperial workshops and magistrate of Yongning County.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Fu loved chivalry and held himself high; through his father's privilege he first became a third-rank attendant, then exchanged to district captain of Yiyang, served as judicial assistant in Mingzhou, and was promoted to construction supervisor of the imperial workshops and magistrate of Yongning County.

sentences.zh: 河南守宋綬薦其材，遷通判儀州，徙慶州。

translations.literal: The Henan prefect Song Shou recommended his talent; he was transferred as vice prefect of Yi Prefecture and moved to Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Henan prefect Song Shou recommended his ability, and he was made vice prefect of Yizhou, then transferred to Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時議進兵西討，以傅督一道糧饋。

translations.literal: At the time the court debated advancing troops in a western punitive campaign; Fu was put in charge of grain supply for one route.
translations.idiomatic: When the court was debating a western punitive advance, Geng Fu was assigned to supervise grain transport along one route.

sentences.zh: 會元昊入寇，參任福行營軍事，遇敵姚家川，諸將失利，敵騎益至，武英勸傅避去，傅不答。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao invaded, he joined Ren Fu's field camp as military staff; they met the enemy at Yaojiachuan, the generals were defeated, enemy horsemen kept arriving, Wu Ying urged Fu to withdraw, and Fu did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao invaded, he served on Ren Fu's field staff; at Yaojiachuan they met the enemy, the generals were beaten, and enemy cavalry kept coming. Wu Ying urged Geng Fu to pull back, but he would not answer.

sentences.zh: 英歎曰：「英當死，君文吏，無軍責，奈何與英俱死？

translations.literal: Ying sighed and said: "Ying ought to die; you are a civil official with no military duty—why should you die together with Ying?
translations.idiomatic: Ying sighed and said, "I am the one who ought to die. You are a civil official with no command responsibility—why should you die with me?

sentences.zh: 」朱觀亦白傅少避賊鋒，而傅愈前，指顧自若，被數創，乃死。

translations.literal: " Zhu Guan also told Fu to sidestep the enemy's spearhead a little, but Fu pressed forward all the more, gesturing and looking about with composure, suffered several wounds, and then died.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhu Guan also urged him to give the enemy's point a little ground, but Geng Fu pressed forward all the more, gesturing and glancing about as calmly as before until he had taken several wounds and died.

sentences.zh: 始，傅與觀營籠落川，夜作書遺福，以其日小勝，前與敵大軍遇，深以持重戒之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Fu and Guan were encamped at Longluo Stream; at night he wrote a letter left for Ren Fu, mentioning the day's small victory and that ahead they would meet the enemy's main force, earnestly warning him to be cautious and steady.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Geng Fu and Zhu Guan were encamped on the Longluo Stream, he wrote at night to Ren Fu. He noted the day's minor success and warned that the main enemy force lay ahead, urging him in the strongest terms to keep his bearing steady.

sentences.zh: 自寫題觀名，以致福軍中。

translations.literal: He wrote it himself and addressed it with Guan's name, and had it delivered into Ren Fu's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote it himself, signed it with Zhu Guan's name, and had it delivered into Ren Fu's camp.

sentences.zh: 傅死後，韓琦得其書於隨軍孔目官彭忠，奏上之。

translations.literal: After Fu died, Han Qi obtained the letter from the camp clerk Peng Zhong who accompanied the army and memorialized it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Geng Fu's death, Han Qi recovered the letter from the camp clerk Peng Zhong and presented it to the throne.

sentences.zh: 詔贈傅右諫議大夫，官其子瑗為太常寺太祝，琚為太常寺奉禮郎，璋為將作監主簿，珪試秘書省校書郎，琬同學究出身。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously awarded Fu the title Right Remonstrance Grand Master and appointed his sons: Yuan as Arch-Sacrificer of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Ju as Court Gentleman of Sacrifices, Zhang as Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings, Gui as probationary Proofreader of the Secretariat, and Wan with the standing of one who had passed the classicist examination.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously enfeoffed Geng Fu as Right Remonstrance Grand Master and appointed his sons Yuan, Ju, Zhang, Gui, and Wan to offices ranging from arch-sacrificer and court gentleman of sacrifices to registrar of the works directorate, probationary secretariat proofreader, and classicist examination standing.

sentences.zh: 王仲寶

translations.literal: Wang Zhongbao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongbao

translations.literal: 〈Appended biography〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appended biography〉

sentences.zh: 王仲寶，字器之，密州高密人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhongbao, styled Qizhi, was a native of Gaomi in Mizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhongbao, courtesy name Qizhi, was from Gaomi in Mizhou.

sentences.zh: 初為刑部史，補齊州章丘尉。

translations.literal: At first he was a clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was appointed sheriff of Zhangqiu in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He began as a clerk in the Ministry of Justice and was appointed sheriff of Zhangqiu in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 以捕群盜六十餘人有功，用開封府判官鞠仲謀薦，召對，改右班殿直，為鎮、定、保、深、永寧、天雄六州軍巡檢。

translations.literal: For merit in capturing more than sixty bandits as a group, on the recommendation of Kaifeng prefectural judge Ju Zhongmou he was summoned to audience, changed to Right Guard Duty Attendant, and made patrol inspector of the six prefectures and armies Zhen, Ding, Bao, Shen, Yongning, and Tianxiong.
translations.idiomatic: After capturing more than sixty bandits together, he was recommended by Kaifeng judge Ju Zhongmou, summoned to audience, made Right Guard Duty Attendant, and appointed patrol inspector over Zhen, Ding, Bao, Shen, Yongning, and Tianxiong.

sentences.zh: 又以捕賊功，遷左班，徙河北西路提舉捉賊，擒磁州名賊王遇仙、博州孫流油輩，凡四十人。

translations.literal: Again for merit in capturing bandits he was promoted to Left Guard Duty Attendant, moved to commissioner for apprehending bandits on the Hebei West circuit, and captured the notorious bandits Wang Yuxian of Cizhou, Sun Liuyou of Bozhou, and their fellows, forty in all.
translations.idiomatic: Further successes against bandits won him promotion to Left Guard Duty Attendant and transfer as Hebei West circuit commissioner for apprehending bandits; he took the notorious Wang Yuxian of Cizhou, Sun Liuyou of Bozhou, and others, forty in all.

sentences.zh: 夜有盜叩戶外乞降，左右欲殺之，為首級論功，仲寶不可，納舍中使寢。

translations.literal: At night a bandit knocked outside the door begging to surrender; his attendants wanted to kill him to claim the head for merit, but Zhongbao would not allow it and took him into quarters to sleep.
translations.idiomatic: One night a bandit knocked at his door begging to surrender; his men wanted to kill him for the head count, but Zhongbao refused, brought him inside, and let him sleep.

sentences.zh: 擢閤門祗候，命乘驛捕登州海賊百餘人，獲之。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Gatehouse Attendant and ordered to travel by post relay to capture more than a hundred sea bandits of Dengzhou; he took them.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Gatehouse Attendant, he was sent by post relay to Dengzhou and captured more than a hundred sea pirates.

sentences.zh: 還，為河北提舉捉賊，又捕斬百餘人。

translations.literal: On his return he became Hebei commissioner for apprehending bandits and again captured and executed more than a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he served again as Hebei commissioner for apprehending bandits and captured and executed more than a hundred more.

sentences.zh: 知信安軍，復為河北提舉捉賊。

translations.literal: He governed Xin'an Army and again served as Hebei commissioner for apprehending bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Xin'an Army, then again served as Hebei commissioner for apprehending bandits.

sentences.zh: 有盜百餘依西山，官軍不能捕，仲寶悉招出，隸軍籍，奏以自隨。

translations.literal: More than a hundred bandits were lodged on the western hills and government troops could not capture them; Zhongbao summoned them all out, enrolled them in the army rolls, and memorialized to keep them with him.
translations.idiomatic: When more than a hundred bandits held the western hills beyond the reach of government troops, Zhongbao induced them all to come out, enrolled them in the army, and memorialized to keep them in his service.

sentences.zh: 徙澤、潞、晉、絳、慈、隰、威勝軍巡檢使，至官才八日，獲太行山宿賊八十人。

translations.literal: He was moved to patrol inspector of Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and Weisheng Army; only eight days after taking office he captured eighty long-established bandits of the Taihang Mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred as patrol inspector over Ze, Lu, Jin, Jiang, Ci, Xi, and Weisheng Army, he had been in office only eight days when he took eighty veteran bandits of the Taihang range.

sentences.zh: 累賜金帛、緡錢。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly rewarded with gold, silk, and strings of cash.
translations.idiomatic: He received repeated gifts of gold, silk, and cash.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，積遷內殿承制。

translations.literal: He served as envoy to the Khitan and was steadily promoted to Inner Palace Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Sent as envoy to the Khitan, he rose step by step to Inner Palace Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 天聖初，知鎮戎軍，改供備庫副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Tiansheng era he governed Zhenrong Army and was changed to Vice Commissioner of the Supply Repository.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Tiansheng reign he governed Zhenrong Army and was made Vice Commissioner of the Supply Repository.

sentences.zh: 破康奴族，獲首領百五十、羊馬七千，詔獎其功。

translations.literal: He defeated the Kangnu tribe, took a hundred fifty chieftains and seven thousand sheep and horses, and an edict praised his achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He broke the Kangnu tribe, took a hundred fifty chieftains and seven thousand sheep and horses, and received an edict commending his achievement.

sentences.zh: 凡五年，還，巡護惠民河堤岸，遷供備庫使、麟府路兵馬鈐轄、知麟州。

translations.literal: After five years in all he returned, patrolled the dikes of the Huimin Canal, and was promoted to Commissioner of the Supply Repository, military superintendent of the Lin-Fu circuit, and prefect of Lin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After five years he returned, inspected the Huimin Canal dikes, and was promoted to Supply Repository Commissioner, military superintendent on the Lin-Fu circuit, and prefect of Linzhou.

sentences.zh: 會鎮戎軍蕃族內寇，徙涇原路鈐轄，復知鎮戎軍，又徙原、環二州。

translations.literal: When the tribes at Zhenrong Army raided within the borders, he was moved to superintendent of the Jingyuan circuit, again governed Zhenrong Army, and was then transferred to the two prefectures Yuan and Huan.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribes at Zhenrong Army rose within the borders, he was transferred as Jingyuan superintendent, again governed Zhenrong Army, and later moved to Yuan and Huan prefectures.

sentences.zh: 以西京左藏庫使、惠州刺史知利州，徙幷代州鈐轄，改西上閤門使。

translations.literal: As Commissioner of the Western Capital Left Treasury and prefect of Huizhou he governed Lizhou; he was moved to superintendent of Bing and Dai prefectures and changed to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: As Western Capital Left Treasury Commissioner and Huizhou prefect he governed Lizhou, then became superintendent of Bing and Dai and Western Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建言：「緣邊博糴，屬羌苦之，數逃去。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Along the border the government grain purchases oppress the subject Qiang; they suffer under it and repeatedly flee.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Along the frontier the government grain-purchase program weighs on the subject Qiang; they suffer under it and keep fleeing.

sentences.zh: 請寬其法，使得復業，以捍邊境。

translations.literal: I ask that the law be relaxed so they may return to their livelihoods and thereby defend the border."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the regulations be eased so they may return to their livelihoods and hold the border for us."

sentences.zh: 」久之，遷東上閤門使。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元昊寇延州，仲寶將兵至賀蘭谷，以分兵勢，敗蕃將羅逋於長雞嶺。

translations.literal: When Yuanhao raided Yan Prefecture, Zhongbao led troops to Helan Valley to divide the enemy's force and defeated the tribal general Luo Bu at Changji Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao attacked Yanzhou, Zhongbao marched to Helan Valley to divide the enemy's strength and defeated the Tangut general Luo Bu at Changji Ridge.

sentences.zh: 遷四方館使，領濮州團練使，為涇原路總管、安撫副使兼管勾秦鳳路軍馬事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commissioner of the Four Diplomatic Hostels, given the nominal rank of regimental commander of Pu Prefecture, and made overall commander of the Jingyuan circuit, vice pacification commissioner, and overseer of Qinfeng circuit military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Commissioner of the Four Diplomatic Hostels, nominal regimental commander of Puzhou, overall commander on the Jingyuan circuit, vice pacification commissioner, and overseer of Qinfeng military affairs.

sentences.zh: 與西羌戰六盤山，俘馘數百人。

translations.literal: He fought the Western Qiang at Liupan Mountain and captured and slew several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Liupan Mountain he fought the Western Qiang and took several hundred prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 時任福大敗好水川，別將朱觀被圍於姚家堡，仲寶以兵救之，拔觀出圍，乘以從馬。

translations.literal: At the time Ren Fu suffered a great defeat at Haoshui Stream; the separate commander Zhu Guan was besieged at Yaojia Fort; Zhongbao led troops to rescue him, pulled Guan out of the encirclement, and gave him a spare horse to ride.
translations.idiomatic: When Ren Fu was routed at Haoshui Stream and Zhu Guan was trapped at Yaojia Fort, Zhongbao fought through to free him from the encirclement and put him on a spare mount.

sentences.zh: 時諸將皆沒，獨仲寶與觀得還。

translations.literal: At the time all the generals perished; only Zhongbao and Guan returned.
translations.idiomatic: By then every other general had been lost; only Zhongbao and Guan made it back.

sentences.zh: 徙環慶路副都總管、知慶州。

translations.literal: He was moved to deputy overall commander of the Huanqing circuit and prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred as deputy overall commander on the Huanqing circuit and prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，兼本路經略安撫、招討副使。

translations.literal: Before long he also held the posts of circuit pacification commissioner and vice commissioner for punitive campaigns on his circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he also served as circuit pacification commissioner and vice commissioner for punitive campaigns.

sentences.zh: 破金湯城，復賜詔獎諭，徙澶州副總管。

translations.literal: He captured Jintang Fortress; again an edict praised and instructed him, and he was moved to deputy overall commander of Chanzou.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jintang Fortress, received another edict of commendation, and was transferred as deputy overall commander at Chanzou.

sentences.zh: 安撫使范仲淹以仲寶武幹未衰，奏留之。

translations.literal: Pacification Commissioner Fan Zhongyan, considering that Zhongbao's martial ability had not declined, memorialized to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Fan Zhongyan, judging that Zhongbao's martial vigor had not waned, memorialized to retain him.

sentences.zh: 明年以磁州防禦使知代州，除左屯衛大將軍致仕，卒。

translations.literal: The next year, as defense commissioner of Cizhou he governed Dai Prefecture; he was granted the title Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard and retired, then died.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he governed Daizhou as Cizhou defense commissioner, was granted Grand General of the Left Garrison Guard and retired, and died.

sentences.zh: 論曰：元昊乘中國弛備，悉眾寇邊，王師大衄者三，夫豈天時不利哉？

translations.literal: The historians comment: Yuanhao seized upon China's slack defenses, led all his forces to raid the border, and the imperial armies suffered three great defeats—was that truly unfavorable timing of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: The historians comment: Yuanhao took advantage of China's slack defenses, threw all his strength against the border, and the imperial armies suffered three crushing defeats—was that truly Heaven's ill favor?

sentences.zh: 亦人謀而已。

translations.literal: It was only human planning after all.
translations.idiomatic: It was human counsel, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 好水之敗，諸將力戰以死。

translations.literal: In the defeat at Haoshui, the generals fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: At Haoshui the generals fought to the last and died.

sentences.zh: 噫，趨利以違節度，固失計矣；

translations.literal: Alas, to rush for gain in violation of command was indeed a mistaken plan;
translations.idiomatic: Alas, to rush for gain against command was folly in itself;

sentences.zh: 然秉義不屈，庶幾烈士者哉！

translations.literal: yet to hold to righteousness and not yield—they might almost be called men of martyred integrity!
translations.idiomatic: yet in holding to righteousness and refusing to yield, were they not almost martyrs!
